subject: Chemistry
question_english: What happens when an acid reacts with a metal? How is the gas evolved tested?
question_hinglish: Acid metal ke saath react kare toh kya hota hai? Nikli gas ki jaanch kaise karte hain?
answer_english: The metal displaces hydrogen from the acid as hydrogen gas and forms a salt: Acid + Metal → Salt + Hydrogen gas. For example, zinc with dilute sulphuric acid gives bubbles on the zinc granules: Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂. When the gas is passed through soap solution, it forms gas-filled bubbles, and a burning candle brought near a bubble shows that the gas burns, confirming hydrogen.
answer_hinglish: Metal acid se hydrogen ko hydrogen gas ke roop mein hata deta hai aur salt banta hai: Acid + Metal → Salt + Hydrogen gas. Jaise zinc dilute sulphuric acid ke saath zinc granules pe bulbule deta hai: Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂. Gas ko sabun ke ghol se guzaarne pe gas bhare bulbule bante hain, aur bulbule ke paas jalti mombatti laane pe gas jalti hai, jo hydrogen ki pushti karti hai.
ncert_context: Take about 5 mL of dilute sulphuric acid in a test tube and add a few pieces of zinc granules to it. What do you observe on the surface of zinc granules? Repeat this Activity with some more acids like HCl, HNO₃ and CH₃COOH. The metal in the above reactions displaces hydrogen atoms from the acids as hydrogen gas and forms a compound called a salt. Thus, the reaction of a metal with an acid can be summarised as – Acid + Metal → Salt + Hydrogen gas. Figure 2.1 shows the reaction of zinc granules with dilute sulphuric acid and testing hydrogen gas by burning.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: How do metal carbonates and hydrogencarbonates react with acids? How is the gas identified?
question_hinglish: Metal carbonates aur hydrogencarbonates acids ke saath kaise react karte hain? Gas ki pehchaan kaise karte hain?
answer_english:
They react with acids to give a salt, carbon dioxide and water:
Na₂CO₃(s) + 2HCl(aq) → 2NaCl(aq) + H₂O(l) + CO₂(g)
NaHCO₃(s) + HCl(aq) → NaCl(aq) + H₂O(l) + CO₂(g)
The gas turns lime water milky by forming a white precipitate of calcium carbonate: Ca(OH)₂(aq) + CO₂(g) → CaCO₃(s) + H₂O(l). With excess CO₂, the milkiness disappears as soluble calcium hydrogencarbonate forms: CaCO₃ + H₂O + CO₂ → Ca(HCO₃)₂.
answer_hinglish:
Yeh acids ke saath react karke salt, carbon dioxide aur paani dete hain:
Na₂CO₃(s) + 2HCl(aq) → 2NaCl(aq) + H₂O(l) + CO₂(g)
NaHCO₃(s) + HCl(aq) → NaCl(aq) + H₂O(l) + CO₂(g)
Gas chuune ke paani ko doodhiya kar deti hai, kyunki calcium carbonate ka safed precipitate banta hai: Ca(OH)₂(aq) + CO₂(g) → CaCO₃(s) + H₂O(l). Zyada CO₂ guzaarne pe ghulne wala calcium hydrogencarbonate banne se doodhiyapan gaayab ho jaata hai: CaCO₃ + H₂O + CO₂ → Ca(HCO₃)₂.
ncert_context: Take about 0.5 g of sodium carbonate in test tube A and about 0.5 g of sodium hydrogencarbonate in test tube B. Add about 2 mL of dilute HCl to both. Pass the gas produced through lime water. Test tube A: Na₂CO₃(s) + 2HCl(aq) → 2NaCl(aq) + H₂O(l) + CO₂(g). Test tube B: NaHCO₃(s) + HCl(aq) → NaCl(aq) + H₂O(l) + CO₂(g). On passing the carbon dioxide gas evolved through lime water, Ca(OH)₂(aq) + CO₂(g) → CaCO₃(s) (white precipitate) + H₂O(l). On passing excess carbon dioxide: CaCO₃(s) + H₂O(l) + CO₂(g) → Ca(HCO₃)₂(aq) (soluble in water). All metal carbonates and hydrogencarbonates react with acids to give a corresponding salt, carbon dioxide and water.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: What is a neutralisation reaction? Explain with phenolphthalein, sodium hydroxide and hydrochloric acid.
question_hinglish: Neutralisation reaction kya hai? Phenolphthalein, sodium hydroxide aur hydrochloric acid se samjhao.
answer_english: A neutralisation reaction is the reaction between an acid and a base to give a salt and water: Base + Acid → Salt + Water. Phenolphthalein added to dilute NaOH turns pink. Adding dilute HCl drop by drop removes the pink colour as the acid nullifies the base: NaOH(aq) + HCl(aq) → NaCl(aq) + H₂O(l). Adding a few drops of NaOH again brings the pink colour back.
answer_hinglish: Neutralisation reaction acid aur base ki aisi reaction hai jisme salt aur paani bante hain: Base + Acid → Salt + Water. Dilute NaOH mein phenolphthalein daalne pe woh gulaabi ho jaata hai. Boond-boond dilute HCl daalne pe acid base ka asar khatam karta hai aur gulaabi rang chala jaata hai: NaOH(aq) + HCl(aq) → NaCl(aq) + H₂O(l). Phir kuch boondein NaOH daalne pe gulaabi rang waapas aa jaata hai.
ncert_context: Take about 2 mL of dilute NaOH solution in a test tube and add two drops of phenolphthalein solution. What is the colour of the solution? Add dilute HCl solution to the above solution drop by drop. Is there any colour change? Now add a few drops of NaOH to the above mixture. Does the pink colour of phenolphthalein reappear? We have observed that the effect of a base is nullified by an acid and vice-versa. The reaction taking place is written as – NaOH(aq) + HCl(aq) → NaCl(aq) + H₂O(l). The reaction between an acid and a base to give a salt and water is known as a neutralisation reaction. In general, a neutralisation reaction can be written as – Base + Acid → Salt + Water.

question_english: 10 mL of an NaOH solution is completely neutralised by 8 mL of an HCl solution. How much of the same HCl solution will neutralise 20 mL of the same NaOH solution?

subject: Chemistry
question_english: Why are metallic oxides called basic oxides and non-metallic oxides called acidic oxides?
question_hinglish: Metallic oxides ko basic oxides aur non-metallic oxides ko acidic oxides kyun kehte hain?
answer_english: Metallic oxides react with acids to give a salt and water, like a base does; for example, copper oxide dissolves in dilute HCl giving a blue-green solution of copper(II) chloride: CuO + 2HCl → CuCl₂ + H₂O. So they are basic oxides. Non-metallic oxides react with bases to give a salt and water, like an acid does; for example, carbon dioxide reacts with calcium hydroxide. So they are acidic in nature.
answer_hinglish: Metallic oxides base ki tarah acids ke saath react karke salt aur paani dete hain; jaise copper oxide dilute HCl mein ghulkar copper(II) chloride ka neela-hara solution deta hai: CuO + 2HCl → CuCl₂ + H₂O. Isliye yeh basic oxides hain. Non-metallic oxides acid ki tarah bases ke saath react karke salt aur paani dete hain; jaise carbon dioxide calcium hydroxide se react karta hai. Isliye yeh acidic hote hain.
ncert_context: Take a small amount of copper oxide in a beaker and add dilute hydrochloric acid slowly while stirring. You will notice that the colour of the solution becomes blue-green and the copper oxide dissolves. The blue-green colour of the solution is due to the formation of copper(II) chloride. The general reaction between a metal oxide and an acid can be written as – Metal oxide + Acid → Salt + Water. Since metallic oxides react with acids to give salts and water, similar to the reaction of a base with an acid, metallic oxides are said to be basic oxides. Calcium hydroxide, which is a base, reacts with carbon dioxide to produce a salt and water. Since this is similar to the reaction between a base and an acid, we can conclude that non-metallic oxides are acidic in nature.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: Why should curd and sour substances not be kept in brass and copper vessels?
question_hinglish: Dahi aur khatti cheezein peetal aur taambe ke bartanon mein kyun nahi rakhni chahiye?
answer_english: Curd and sour substances contain acids, such as lactic acid in curd. Acids react with metals to form salts, so they would react with the copper in brass and copper vessels, spoiling the food and damaging the vessel.
answer_hinglish: Dahi aur khatti cheezon mein acids hote hain, jaise dahi mein lactic acid. Acids metals ke saath react karke salts banate hain, isliye woh peetal aur taambe ke bartanon ke copper se react karenge, jisse khaana kharaab hoga aur bartan ko nuksaan pahunchega.

Thus, the reaction of a metal with an acid can be summarised as – Acid + Metal → Salt + Hydrogen gas. Acids are sour in taste. subject: Chemistry
question_english: Why do HCl and HNO₃ show acidic character in water, while alcohol and glucose solutions do not, even though all contain hydrogen?
question_hinglish: HCl aur HNO₃ paani mein acidic gun kyun dikhaate hain, jabki alcohol aur glucose ke solutions nahi, halaanki sabme hydrogen hai?
answer_english: Acids like HCl and HNO₃ produce hydrogen ions, H⁺(aq), in water, which are responsible for acidic properties, and these ions carry electric current, so a bulb glows when current is passed through their solutions. Glucose and alcohol also contain hydrogen but do not produce H⁺ ions in water, so their solutions do not conduct electricity and do not show acidic character.
answer_hinglish: HCl aur HNO₃ jaise acids paani mein hydrogen ions, H⁺(aq), banate hain jo acidic gunon ke liye zimmedar hain, aur yeh ions bijli le jaate hain, isliye unke solution se current guzaarne pe bulb jalta hai. Glucose aur alcohol mein bhi hydrogen hai par woh paani mein H⁺ ions nahi banate, isliye unke solutions bijli conduct nahi karte aur acidic gun nahi dikhaate.
ncert_context: Take solutions of glucose, alcohol, hydrochloric acid and sulphuric acid. Fix two nails on a cork in a beaker connected to a 6 volt battery through a bulb and a switch. The bulb will start glowing in the case of acids. But glucose and alcohol solutions do not conduct electricity. Glowing of the bulb indicates that there is a flow of electric current through the solution. The electric current is carried through the acidic solution by ions. Acids contain H⁺ ion as cation and anion such as Cl⁻ in HCl, NO₃⁻ in HNO₃, SO₄²⁻ in H₂SO₄, CH₃COO⁻ in CH₃COOH. Since the cation present in acids is H⁺, this suggests that acids produce hydrogen ions, H⁺(aq), in solution, which are responsible for their acidic properties.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: Why does dry HCl gas not change the colour of dry litmus paper, while it changes wet litmus paper?
question_hinglish: Sukhi HCl gas sukhe litmus paper ka rang kyun nahi badalti, jabki geele litmus ka badal deti hai?
answer_english: Hydrogen ions in HCl are produced only in the presence of water; H⁺ cannot separate from HCl molecules without water. So dry HCl gas gives no H⁺ ions and does not affect dry blue litmus. On wet litmus, the water lets HCl form ions: HCl + H₂O → H₃O⁺ + Cl⁻, and the litmus turns red. H⁺ ions do not exist alone; they combine with water to form hydronium ions, H₃O⁺.
answer_hinglish: HCl mein hydrogen ions sirf paani ki maujoodgi mein bante hain; bina paani ke H⁺ HCl molecules se alag nahi ho sakta. Isliye sukhi HCl gas H⁺ ions nahi deti aur sukhe neele litmus pe asar nahi karti. Geele litmus pe paani ki wajah se HCl ions banata hai: HCl + H₂O → H₃O⁺ + Cl⁻, aur litmus laal ho jaata hai. H⁺ ions akele nahi rehte; woh paani se judkar hydronium ions, H₃O⁺, banate hain.
ncert_context: Take about 1 g solid NaCl in a dry test tube and add some concentrated sulphuric acid. Test the gas evolved successively with dry and wet blue litmus paper. In which case does the litmus paper change colour? What do you infer about the acidic character of dry HCl gas and HCl solution? This experiment suggests that hydrogen ions in HCl are produced in the presence of water. The separation of H⁺ ion from HCl molecules cannot occur in the absence of water. HCl + H₂O → H₃O⁺ + Cl⁻. Hydrogen ions cannot exist alone, but they exist after combining with water molecules. Thus hydrogen ions must always be shown as H⁺(aq) or hydronium ion (H₃O⁺). H⁺ + H₂O → H₃O⁺.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: What are alkalis? What ions do bases produce in water?
question_hinglish: Alkalis kya hain? Bases paani mein kaun se ions banate hain?
answer_english: Bases produce hydroxide ions, OH⁻(aq), in water; for example, NaOH(s) → Na⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq) and Mg(OH)₂(s) → Mg²⁺(aq) + 2OH⁻(aq). Bases that are soluble in water are called alkalis. Not all bases dissolve in water. Alkalis are soapy to touch, bitter and corrosive, so they should never be tasted or touched.
answer_hinglish: Bases paani mein hydroxide ions, OH⁻(aq), banate hain; jaise NaOH(s) → Na⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq) aur Mg(OH)₂(s) → Mg²⁺(aq) + 2OH⁻(aq). Paani mein ghulne wale bases alkalis kehlaate hain. Saare bases paani mein nahi ghulte. Alkalis chhoone mein saabun jaise, kadve aur corrosive hote hain, isliye inhe kabhi chakhna ya chhoona nahi chahiye.
ncert_context: Let us see what happens when a base is dissolved in water. NaOH(s) → Na⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq) (in water). KOH(s) → K⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq). Mg(OH)₂(s) → Mg²⁺(aq) + 2OH⁻(aq). Bases generate hydroxide (OH⁻) ions in water. Bases which are soluble in water are called alkalis. All bases do not dissolve in water. An alkali is a base that dissolves in water. They are soapy to touch, bitter and corrosive. Never taste or touch them as they may cause harm. Formation of OH⁻(aq) ions in solution is responsible for the basic nature of a substance.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: While diluting an acid, why should the acid be added to water and not water to the acid?
question_hinglish: Acid ko patla karte waqt acid ko paani mein kyun daalna chahiye, paani ko acid mein kyun nahi?
answer_english: Dissolving an acid in water is a highly exothermic process. If water is added to a concentrated acid, the heat generated may make the mixture splash out and cause burns, and the glass container may break from excessive local heating. So the acid must always be added slowly to water with constant stirring.
answer_hinglish: Acid ko paani mein gholna bahut exothermic prakriya hai. Agar gaadhe acid mein paani daala jaaye, toh bani garmi se mixture uchhal kar jala sakta hai, aur zyada local garmi se kaanch ka bartan toot sakta hai. Isliye acid ko hamesha dheere-dheere lagaataar hilaate hue paani mein daalna chahiye.

question_english: What is dilution? How does it affect the concentration of hydronium ions in an acid, and of hydroxide ions when excess base is dissolved in NaOH solution?
question_hinglish: Dilution kya hai? Acid mein hydronium ions ki concentration, aur NaOH solution mein zyada base gholne pe hydroxide ions ki concentration pe iska kya asar hota hai?
answer_english: Dilution is mixing an acid or base with water, which decreases the concentration of ions (H₃O⁺ or OH⁻) per unit volume. So diluting an acid lowers its hydronium ion concentration. question_english: Why does distilled water not conduct electricity, whereas rain water does?
question_hinglish: Distilled water bijli conduct kyun nahi karta, jabki baarish ka paani karta hai?
answer_english: Electric current is carried through a solution by ions. Distilled water is pure and has almost no ions, so it does not conduct. subject: Chemistry
question_english: What is the pH scale? How does pH relate to hydrogen ion concentration?
question_hinglish: pH scale kya hai? pH ka hydrogen ion concentration se kya sambandh hai?
answer_english: The pH scale measures the hydrogen ion concentration in a solution, generally from 0 (very acidic) to 14 (very alkaline); the p stands for 'potenz', German for power. A neutral solution has pH 7, values below 7 are acidic and values above 7 are basic. The higher the hydronium ion concentration, the lower the pH. From 7 to 14, OH⁻ concentration and alkali strength increase. pH is usually measured with paper soaked in universal indicator, a mixture of several indicators.
answer_hinglish: pH scale solution mein hydrogen ion concentration naapta hai, aam taur pe 0 (bahut acidic) se 14 (bahut alkaline) tak; p ka matlab German shabd 'potenz', yaani power. Neutral solution ka pH 7 hai, 7 se kam acidic aur 7 se zyada basic. Hydronium ion concentration jitni zyada, pH utna kam. 7 se 14 tak OH⁻ concentration aur alkali ki taakat badhti hai. pH aam taur pe universal indicator, yaani kai indicators ke mixture, mein bheege paper se naapa jaata hai.
ncert_context: We can find the strength of an acid or base by making use of a universal indicator, which is a mixture of several indicators. The universal indicator shows different colours at different concentrations of hydrogen ions in a solution. A scale for measuring hydrogen ion concentration in a solution, called pH scale has been developed. The p in pH stands for 'potenz' in German, meaning power. On the pH scale we can measure pH generally from 0 (very acidic) to 14 (very alkaline). Higher the hydronium ion concentration, lower is the pH value. The pH of a neutral solution is 7. Values less than 7 on the pH scale represent an acidic solution. As the pH value increases from 7 to 14, it represents an increase in OH⁻ ion concentration in the solution, that is, increase in the strength of alkali. Generally paper impregnated with the universal indicator is used for measuring pH.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: Why is pH important for living organisms? What is acid rain and how does it affect aquatic life?
question_hinglish: Jeevit praaniyon ke liye pH kyun mahatvapurn hai? Acid rain kya hai aur yeh jaliya jeevon ko kaise prabhaavit karti hai?
answer_english: Living organisms can survive only within a narrow range of pH change; our body works within pH 7.0 to 7.8. When the pH of rain water is less than 5.6, it is called acid rain. Paudhon ko bhi achhi badhat ke liye mitti ka ek khaas pH chahiye.

question_english: How do antacids relieve indigestion? Which medicine is used for indigestion?

subject: Chemistry
question_english: How does a change in pH cause tooth decay, and how can it be prevented?
question_hinglish: pH mein badlav se daant kaise sadte hain, aur ise kaise roka ja sakta hai?
answer_english: Tooth decay starts when the pH of the mouth falls below 5.5. Tooth enamel, made of calcium hydroxyapatite, is the hardest substance in the body and does not dissolve in water, but it is corroded below pH 5.5. Bacteria in the mouth produce acids by breaking down sugar and food particles left after eating. Cleaning the mouth after eating and using toothpastes, which are generally basic, neutralise the excess acid and prevent decay.
answer_hinglish: Daant sadna tab shuru hota hai jab muh ka pH 5.5 se neeche chala jaaye. Daant ka enamel, jo calcium hydroxyapatite se bana hai, shareer ka sabse sakht padaarth hai aur paani mein nahi ghulta, par pH 5.5 se neeche ghisne lagta hai. Muh ke bacteria khaane ke baad bache sugar aur khaane ke tukdon ko todkar acid banate hain. Khaane ke baad muh saaf karna aur aam taur pe basic toothpaste use karna extra acid ko neutralise karke daanton ko bachaata hai.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: How can the pain of a bee sting or a nettle sting be relieved?
question_hinglish: Madhumakkhi ke dank ya nettle ke dank ka dard kaise kam kiya ja sakta hai?
answer_english: A bee sting leaves an acid that causes pain and irritation; applying a mild base like baking soda neutralises it and gives relief. Nettle leaves have stinging hair that inject methanoic acid, causing burning pain; the traditional remedy is rubbing the area with a dock leaf, which often grows beside nettle, so the dock plant must be basic in nature.
answer_hinglish: Madhumakkhi ka dank ek acid chhodta hai jo dard aur jalan karta hai; baking soda jaisa halka base lagaane se woh neutralise hota hai aur raahat milti hai. subject: Chemistry
question_english: Fresh milk has pH 6. How will its pH change as it turns into curd? Why does a milkman add a little baking soda to fresh milk, and why does such milk take longer to set as curd?
question_hinglish: Taaze doodh ka pH 6 hai. Dahi banne pe uska pH kaise badlega? Doodhwala taaze doodh mein thoda baking soda kyun milaata hai, aur aisa doodh dahi banne mein zyada samay kyun leta hai?
answer_english: As milk turns into curd, lactic acid forms, so the pH decreases below 6 and it becomes more acidic. The milkman adds a little baking soda, a mild base, to shift the pH to slightly alkaline so the milk does not turn sour quickly. Such milk takes longer to set as curd because the acid produced must first neutralise the added base before the milk becomes acidic enough to curdle.
answer_hinglish: Doodh ke dahi banne pe lactic acid banta hai, isliye pH 6 se neeche girta hai aur woh zyada acidic hota hai. Doodhwala halka base baking soda milakar pH thoda alkaline kar deta hai taaki doodh jaldi khatta na ho. Aisa doodh dahi banne mein zyada samay leta hai kyunki bana acid pehle milaaye gaye base ko neutralise karta hai, tabhi doodh jamne layak acidic ho paata hai.
ncert_context: Table 2.3: Sour milk (curd) contains lactic acid. Higher the hydronium ion concentration, lower is the pH value. subject: Chemistry
question_english: Under what soil condition would a farmer treat the fields with quick lime, slaked lime or chalk?
question_hinglish: Kisan kis mitti ki sthiti mein khet mein quick lime, slaked lime ya chalk daalega?
answer_english: A farmer would use quick lime (calcium oxide), slaked lime (calcium hydroxide) or chalk (calcium carbonate) when the soil is too acidic. These are basic substances that neutralise the excess acid and bring the soil to the pH range plants need for healthy growth.
answer_hinglish: Jab mitti bahut acidic ho, tab kisan quick lime (calcium oxide), slaked lime (calcium hydroxide) ya chalk (calcium carbonate) daalega. Yeh basic padaarth extra acid ko neutralise karke mitti ko paudhon ki achhi badhat ke liye zaroori pH tak laate hain.
ncert_context: Plants require a specific pH range for their healthy growth. Put about 2 g soil in a test tube, add 5 mL water, shake, filter and check the pH of the filtrate with universal indicator paper. Calcium oxide is called lime or quick lime. Calcium oxide reacts with water to produce slaked lime (calcium hydroxide). Limestone, chalk and marble are different forms of calcium carbonate. Metal carbonates react with acids to give a salt, carbon dioxide and water. Acids and bases neutralise each other.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: What is a family of salts? How does the pH of a salt depend on the acid and base it is formed from?
question_hinglish: Salts ka family kya hota hai? Salt ka pH us acid aur base pe kaise nirbhar karta hai jinse woh bana hai?
answer_english: Salts with the same positive or negative radical belong to a family; NaCl and Na₂SO₄ belong to the family of sodium salts, and NaCl and KCl to the family of chloride salts. Salts of a strong acid and strong base are neutral with pH 7, like sodium chloride. Salts of a strong acid and weak base are acidic (pH below 7), and salts of a strong base and weak acid are basic (pH above 7).

Strong acid aur weak base ke salts acidic (pH 7 se kam), aur strong base aur weak acid ke salts basic (pH 7 se zyada) hote hain.
ncert_context: Salts having the same positive or negative radicals are said to belong to a family. For example, NaCl and Na₂SO₄ belong to the family of sodium salts. On the other hand, salts of a strong acid and weak base are acidic with pH value less than 7 and those of a strong base and weak acid are basic in nature, with pH value more than 7. The salt formed by the combination of hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide solution is called sodium chloride; it is a neutral salt.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: What is the chlor-alkali process? Name its products and where each is formed.
question_hinglish: Chlor-alkali process kya hai? Iske products aur har ek kahan banta hai, batao.
answer_english:
When electricity is passed through brine (an aqueous solution of sodium chloride), it decomposes:
2NaCl(aq) + 2H₂O(l) → 2NaOH(aq) + Cl₂(g) + H₂(g)
Chlorine gas is given off at the anode, hydrogen gas at the cathode, and sodium hydroxide solution forms near the cathode. It is called chlor-alkali because it produces chlorine and an alkali (sodium hydroxide). All three products are useful.
answer_hinglish:
Brine (sodium chloride ka aqueous solution) mein bijli guzaarne pe woh toot-ta hai:
2NaCl(aq) + 2H₂O(l) → 2NaOH(aq) + Cl₂(g) + H₂(g)
Chlorine gas anode pe, hydrogen gas cathode pe nikalti hai, aur sodium hydroxide solution cathode ke paas banta hai. Ise chlor-alkali isliye kehte hain kyunki yeh chlorine aur ek alkali (sodium hydroxide) banata hai. Teeno products upyogi hain.

question_hinglish: Bleaching powder kaise banta hai, aur iske kya upyog hain?
answer_english:
Bleaching powder is made by the action of chlorine (from the chlor-alkali process) on dry slaked lime:
2Ca(OH)₂ + 2Cl₂ → Ca(OCl)₂ + CaCl₂ + 2H₂O
It is represented as Ca(OCl)₂, though its actual composition is complex. It is used to bleach cotton and linen in the textile industry, wood pulp in paper factories and washed clothes in laundry; as an oxidising agent in chemical industries; and to make drinking water free from germs.
answer_hinglish:

Ise Ca(OCl)₂ likhte hain, halaanki asli banaavat pecheeda hai. Iska use textile udyog mein cotton aur linen, kaagaz factories mein lakdi ki lugdi, aur laundry mein dhule kapdon ko bleach karne; chemical industries mein oxidising agent ki tarah; aur peene ke paani ko keetanu-mukt karne mein hota hai.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: How is baking soda made? What happens when it is heated, and what are its uses?
question_hinglish: Baking soda kaise banta hai? Garam karne pe kya hota hai, aur iske kya upyog hain?
answer_english:
Baking soda, sodium hydrogencarbonate (NaHCO₃), is made using sodium chloride as a raw material:
NaCl + H₂O + CO₂ + NH₃ → NH₄Cl + NaHCO₃
On heating during cooking: 2NaHCO₃ → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂
It is a mild, non-corrosive basic salt. Uses: in baking powder (with tartaric acid), where CO₂ makes cakes soft and spongy; in antacids to neutralise excess stomach acid; and in soda-acid fire extinguishers.
answer_hinglish:
Baking soda, sodium hydrogencarbonate (NaHCO₃), sodium chloride ko kachche maal ki tarah use karke banta hai:
NaCl + H₂O + CO₂ + NH₃ → NH₄Cl + NaHCO₃
Khaana banate waqt garam karne pe: 2NaHCO₃ → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂
Yeh halka, non-corrosive basic salt hai. Upyog: baking powder mein (tartaric acid ke saath), jahan CO₂ cake ko naram aur spongy banata hai; pet ka extra acid neutralise karne wale antacids mein; aur soda-acid fire extinguishers mein.
ncert_context: The chemical name of baking soda is sodium hydrogencarbonate (NaHCO₃). It is produced using sodium chloride as one of the raw materials: NaCl + H₂O + CO₂ + NH₃ → NH₄Cl + NaHCO₃. It is a mild non-corrosive basic salt. The following reaction takes place when it is heated during cooking – 2NaHCO₃ → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂ (on heating). Uses of baking soda: (i) Baking powder is a mixture of baking soda and tartaric acid, a weak edible acid. When baking powder is heated or mixed in water, carbon dioxide produced can cause bread or cake to rise making them soft and spongy. (ii) Sodium hydrogencarbonate is also an ingredient in antacids. Being alkaline, it neutralises excess acid in the stomach. (iii) It is also used in soda-acid fire extinguishers.

question_english: How is washing soda obtained? Give its uses.
question_hinglish: Washing soda kaise milta hai? Iske upyog batao.
answer_english:
Heating baking soda gives sodium carbonate, and recrystallising sodium carbonate gives washing soda, Na₂CO₃·10H₂O, a basic salt: Na₂CO₃ + 10H₂O → Na₂CO₃·10H₂O.
Uses:
1. In the glass, soap and paper industries.
2. In making sodium compounds such as borax.
3. As a cleaning agent at home.
4. For removing permanent hardness of water.

Upyog:
1. Kaanch, saabun aur kaagaz udyogon mein.
2. Borax jaise sodium compounds banane mein.
3. Ghar mein safaai ke liye.
4. Paani ki permanent hardness hataane ke liye.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: What is water of crystallisation? Explain with copper sulphate crystals.
question_hinglish: Water of crystallisation kya hai? Copper sulphate crystals se samjhao.
answer_english: Water of crystallisation is the fixed number of water molecules present in one formula unit of a salt. Copper sulphate crystals that look dry actually contain water: hydrated copper sulphate is CuSO₄·5H₂O, with five water molecules. On heating, this water is removed, water droplets appear in the tube, and the salt turns white. Adding a few drops of water brings back the blue colour.
answer_hinglish: Water of crystallisation kisi salt ki ek formula unit mein maujood paani ke molecules ki fixed sankhya hai. Sukhe dikhne wale copper sulphate crystals mein asal mein paani hota hai: hydrated copper sulphate CuSO₄·5H₂O hai, jisme paani ke paanch molecules hain. Garam karne pe yeh paani nikal jaata hai, tube mein boondein dikhti hain, aur salt safed ho jaata hai. Kuch boondein paani daalne pe neela rang waapas aa jaata hai.
ncert_context: Heat a few crystals of copper sulphate in a dry boiling tube. What is the colour of the copper sulphate after heating? Do you notice water droplets in the boiling tube? Add 2-3 drops of water on the sample of copper sulphate obtained after heating. Is the blue colour of copper sulphate restored? Copper sulphate crystals which seem to be dry contain water of crystallisation. When we heat the crystals, this water is removed and the salt turns white. If you moisten the crystals again with water, you will find that blue colour of the crystals reappears. Water of crystallisation is the fixed number of water molecules present in one formula unit of a salt. Five water molecules are present in one formula unit of copper sulphate. Chemical formula for hydrated copper sulphate is CuSO₄·5H₂O.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: How is Plaster of Paris prepared from gypsum? What happens when it is mixed with water, and what is it used for?
question_hinglish: Gypsum se Plaster of Paris kaise banta hai? Paani milaane pe kya hota hai, aur iska upyog kya hai?
answer_english:
Gypsum, CaSO₄·2H₂O, on heating at 373 K loses water and becomes calcium sulphate hemihydrate, CaSO₄·½H₂O, called Plaster of Paris. It is a white powder; mixed with water it changes back to gypsum, setting into a hard solid mass:
CaSO₄·½H₂O + 1½H₂O → CaSO₄·2H₂O
Half a water molecule is written because two formula units of CaSO₄ share one water molecule. Doctors use it to support fractured bones; it is also used for toys, decorative materials and smoothing surfaces.
answer_hinglish:
Gypsum, CaSO₄·2H₂O, ko 373 K pe garam karne se woh paani khokar calcium sulphate hemihydrate, CaSO₄·½H₂O, ban jaata hai, jise Plaster of Paris kehte hain. Yeh safed powder hai; paani milaane pe phir gypsum bankar sakht thos mein jam jaata hai:
CaSO₄·½H₂O + 1½H₂O → CaSO₄·2H₂O
Aadha paani ka molecule isliye likhte hain kyunki CaSO₄ ki do formula units ek paani ka molecule share karti hain. Doctor ise tooti haddiyon ko sahara dene mein use karte hain; yeh khilaune, sajaavat ka saamaan aur satah chikni karne mein bhi use hota hai.

question_english: A solution reacts with crushed egg shells to give a gas that turns lime water milky. The solution contains: (a) NaCl (b) HCl (c) LiCl (d) KCl

subject: Chemistry
question_english: How does a soda-acid fire extinguisher work?
question_hinglish: Soda-acid fire extinguisher kaise kaam karta hai?
answer_english: It uses the reaction of an acid with a metal hydrogencarbonate. When dilute sulphuric acid mixes with sodium hydrogencarbonate solution, carbon dioxide is produced, which forces the discharge out of the nozzle. Directed at a fire, such as a burning candle, the carbon dioxide puts it out.
answer_hinglish: Yeh acid aur metal hydrogencarbonate ki reaction use karta hai. Dilute sulphuric acid ke sodium hydrogencarbonate solution se milne pe carbon dioxide banti hai, jo nozzle se dhaar ko bahar dhakelti hai. Aag, jaise jalti mombatti, pe daalne pe carbon dioxide use bujha deti hai.
ncert_context: The reaction of acids with metal hydrogencarbonates is used in the fire extinguishers which produce carbon dioxide. Take 20 mL of sodium hydrogencarbonate (NaHCO₃) solution in a wash-bottle. Suspend an ignition tube containing dilute sulphuric acid in the wash-bottle. Close the mouth of the wash-bottle. Tilt the wash-bottle so that the acid from the ignition tube mixes with the sodium hydrogencarbonate solution below. You will notice discharge coming out of the nozzle. Direct this discharge on a burning candle. Sodium hydrogencarbonate is also used in soda-acid fire extinguishers. The gas evolved from a carbonate and acid extinguishes a burning candle.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: List the general physical properties of metals.
question_hinglish: Metals ke saamaanya physical gun batao.
answer_english:
1. Metallic lustre: pure metals have a shining surface.
2. Metals are generally hard, though hardness varies.
3. Malleability: they can be beaten into thin sheets; gold and silver are the most malleable.
4. Ductility: they can be drawn into thin wires; gold is the most ductile.
5. They are good conductors of heat and electricity and have high melting points.
6. They are sonorous, producing a sound when struck.
answer_hinglish:
1. Metallic lustre: shuddh metals ki satah chamakdaar hoti hai.
2. Metals aam taur pe kathor hote hain, par kathorta alag-alag hoti hai.
3. Malleability: inhe peet kar patli chaadar banaayi ja sakti hai; gold aur silver sabse zyada malleable hain.
4. Ductility: inhe kheench kar patle taar banaaye ja sakte hain; gold sabse zyada ductile hai.
5. Yeh garmi aur bijli ke achhe conductor hain aur inka melting point ooncha hota hai.
6. Yeh sonorous hain, yaani takraane pe aawaaz karte hain.
ncert_context: Metals, in their pure state, have a shining surface. This property is called metallic lustre. Metals are generally hard. The hardness varies from metal to metal. Some metals can be beaten into thin sheets. This property is called malleability. Gold and silver are the most malleable metals. The ability of metals to be drawn into thin wires is called ductility. Gold is the most ductile metal. Metals are good conductors of heat and have high melting points. The metals that produce a sound on striking a hard surface are said to be sonorous. Metals are lustrous, malleable, ductile and are good conductors of heat and electricity.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: Why can't elements be classified as metals and non-metals on physical properties alone? Give the exceptions.
question_hinglish: Elements ko sirf physical gunon se metals aur non-metals mein kyun nahi baanta ja sakta? Apvaad batao.
answer_english:
There are many exceptions:
1. All metals are solids except mercury, a liquid; gallium and caesium melt on the palm despite metals usually having high melting points.
2. Iodine is a non-metal but is lustrous.
3. Diamond, an allotrope of carbon, is the hardest natural substance with very high melting and boiling points, and graphite conducts electricity.
4. Alkali metals (lithium, sodium, potassium) are soft enough to cut with a knife and have low densities and melting points.
So chemical properties classify them more clearly.
answer_hinglish:
Kai apvaad hain:
1. Mercury ke alaava saare metals solid hain; gallium aur caesium hatheli pe pighal jaate hain, jabki metals ka melting point aam taur pe ooncha hota hai.
2. Iodine non-metal hai par chamakdaar hai.
3. Carbon ka allotrope diamond sabse kathor natural padaarth hai jiske melting aur boiling point bahut oonche hain, aur graphite bijli conduct karta hai.
4. Alkali metals (lithium, sodium, potassium) chaaku se kat jaate hain aur inki density aur melting point kam hote hain.
Isliye chemical gun inhe zyada saaf baant-te hain.

(iv) Alkali metals (lithium, sodium, potassium) are so soft that they can be cut with a knife. They have low densities and low melting points. Elements can be more clearly classified as metals and non-metals on the basis of their chemical properties.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: Using a hammer, a battery, a bulb, wires and a switch, how can you distinguish metals from non-metals? How useful are these tests?
question_hinglish: Hathoda, battery, bulb, taar aur switch se metals aur non-metals ko kaise alag pehchanoge? Yeh tests kitne upyogi hain?
answer_english:
Hammer test: strike the sample; a metal flattens into a sheet (malleable), while a non-metal like sulphur or coal breaks or crumbles.
Conductivity test: place the sample in a circuit with the battery, bulb and switch; the bulb glows for a metal but not for most non-metals.
These tests help, but not always: graphite, a non-metal, conducts electricity, and some metals such as sodium are soft. Chemical properties classify elements more clearly.

Yeh tests madad karte hain, par hamesha nahi: non-metal graphite bijli conduct karta hai, aur sodium jaise kuch metals naram hain. Chemical gun elements ko zyada saaf baant-te hain.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: What happens when the products of burning magnesium and burning sulphur are dissolved in water and tested with litmus? What does this show?
question_hinglish: Jalte magnesium aur jalte sulphur ke products ko paani mein gholkar litmus se test karne pe kya hota hai? Isse kya pata chalta hai?
answer_english: Magnesium burns to form magnesium oxide, which dissolves in water to give a basic solution that turns red litmus blue (2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO; MgO + H₂O → Mg(OH)₂). Sulphur burns to form sulphur dioxide, which dissolves in water to give an acidic solution that turns blue litmus red. This shows that most metals form basic oxides, while most non-metals form acidic oxides.

Sulphur jalkar sulphur dioxide banata hai, jo paani mein ghulkar acidic solution deta hai jo neele litmus ko laal karta hai. Isse pata chalta hai ki zyadatar metals basic oxides aur zyadatar non-metals acidic oxides banate hain.
ncert_context: Take a magnesium ribbon and some sulphur powder. Burn the magnesium ribbon. Collect the ashes formed and dissolve them in water. Most non-metals produce acidic oxides when dissolved in water. On the other hand, most metals give rise to basic oxides.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: Do all metals react with oxygen at the same rate? Why is sodium kept immersed in kerosene oil?
question_hinglish: Kya saare metals oxygen ke saath ek hi raftaar se react karte hain? Sodium ko kerosene tel mein dubakar kyun rakhte hain?
answer_english: No, metals show different reactivities towards oxygen. Potassium and sodium react so vigorously that they catch fire if kept in the open, so they are kept immersed in kerosene oil to protect them and prevent accidental fires. Magnesium, aluminium, zinc and lead get a thin protective oxide layer. Iron does not burn on heating, though iron filings burn in a flame; copper does not burn but gets a black oxide coating; silver and gold do not react with oxygen even at high temperatures.
answer_hinglish: Nahi, alag metals oxygen ke saath alag reactivity dikhaate hain. Potassium aur sodium itni tezi se react karte hain ki khule mein rakhne pe aag pakad lete hain, isliye unhe bachaane aur aag se bachne ke liye kerosene tel mein dubakar rakhte hain. Magnesium, aluminium, zinc aur lead pe oxide ki patli suraksha parat ban jaati hai. Iron garam karne pe nahi jalta, par iron ka buraada lau mein jalta hai; copper nahi jalta par uspe kaali oxide parat chadh jaati hai; silver aur gold oonche temperature pe bhi oxygen se react nahi karte.

The protective oxide layer prevents the metal from further oxidation. Iron does not burn on heating but iron filings burn vigorously when sprinkled in the flame of the burner. Copper does not burn, but the hot metal is coated with a black coloured layer of copper(II) oxide. Silver and gold do not react with oxygen even at high temperatures.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: What is anodising? Why is aluminium used for cooking utensils even though it is highly reactive?
question_hinglish: Anodising kya hai? Aluminium bahut reactive hone ke baavjood khaana banane ke bartanon mein kyun use hota hai?
answer_english: Aluminium gets a thin oxide layer in air that resists further corrosion. Anodising makes this layer thicker: a clean aluminium article is made the anode and electrolysed with dilute sulphuric acid, and the oxygen evolved at the anode reacts with aluminium to form a thicker protective oxide layer, which can also be dyed. Because this oxide layer stops further reaction, aluminium can safely be used for cooking utensils, and it is a good conductor of heat.
answer_hinglish: Hawa mein aluminium pe oxide ki patli parat ban jaati hai jo aage corrosion rokti hai. Anodising is parat ko mota karta hai: saaf aluminium ki cheez ko anode banakar dilute sulphuric acid ke saath electrolyse kiya jaata hai, aur anode pe nikli oxygen aluminium ke saath react karke moti suraksha oxide parat banaati hai, jise rang bhi sakte hain. Yeh oxide parat aage reaction rokti hai, isliye aluminium khaana banane ke bartanon mein surakshit hai, aur yeh garmi ka achha conductor bhi hai.
ncert_context: Anodising is a process of forming a thick oxide layer of aluminium. Aluminium develops a thin oxide layer when exposed to air. This aluminium oxide coat makes it resistant to further corrosion. The resistance can be improved further by making the oxide layer thicker. During anodising, a clean aluminium article is made the anode and is electrolysed with dilute sulphuric acid. The oxygen gas evolved at the anode reacts with aluminium to make a thicker protective oxide layer. This oxide layer can be dyed easily to give aluminium articles an attractive finish. The protective oxide layer prevents the metal from further oxidation. Metals are good conductors of heat.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: How do different metals react with water? Compare sodium, calcium, magnesium, aluminium, iron and copper.
question_hinglish: Alag metals paani ke saath kaise react karte hain? Sodium, calcium, magnesium, aluminium, iron aur copper ki tulna karo.
answer_english:
Metals react with water to form a metal oxide (or hydroxide) and hydrogen.
Sodium and potassium react violently with cold water; the hydrogen catches fire: 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂ + heat.
Calcium reacts less violently and floats as hydrogen bubbles stick to it: Ca + 2H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ + H₂.
Magnesium reacts only with hot water, and also floats.
Aluminium, iron and zinc react only with steam: 3Fe + 4H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + 4H₂.
Lead, copper, silver and gold do not react with water at all.
answer_hinglish:

question_english: How do metals react with dilute hydrochloric acid? Arrange magnesium, aluminium, zinc, iron and copper by reactivity.
question_hinglish: Metals dilute hydrochloric acid ke saath kaise react karte hain? Magnesium, aluminium, zinc, iron aur copper ko reactivity ke kram mein lagao.
answer_english: Metals react with dilute acids to give a salt and hydrogen gas: Metal + Dilute acid → Salt + Hydrogen. question_english: Why is hydrogen gas usually not evolved when a metal reacts with nitric acid?
question_hinglish: Metal ke nitric acid ke saath react karne pe aam taur pe hydrogen gas kyun nahi nikalti?
answer_english: Nitric acid is a strong oxidising agent. It oxidises the hydrogen produced to water and itself gets reduced to nitrogen oxides (N₂O, NO or NO₂). Only magnesium and manganese react with very dilute nitric acid to evolve hydrogen gas.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: A man posing as a goldsmith dipped dull gold bangles in a solution; they sparkled like new but lost a lot of weight. What solution did he use?
question_hinglish: Sunar bankar aaye ek aadmi ne feeki gold ki chudiyon ko ek solution mein duba diya; woh nayi jaisi chamakne lagi par unka wazan bahut ghat gaya. Usne kaun sa solution use kiya?
answer_english: He used aqua regia, a freshly prepared mixture of concentrated hydrochloric acid and concentrated nitric acid in the ratio 3:1. It can dissolve gold, though neither acid can alone. It dissolved the dull outer layer of gold, exposing a shiny surface, but the dissolved gold reduced the weight of the bangles.
answer_hinglish: Usne aqua regia use kiya, jo gaadhe hydrochloric acid aur gaadhe nitric acid ka 3:1 anupaat mein taaza bana mixture hai. Yeh gold ko ghol sakta hai, jabki akele koi bhi acid nahi ghol sakta. Isne gold ki feeki bahari parat ghol di, jisse chamakdaar satah dikhi, par ghula gold chudiyon ka wazan ghata gaya.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: What is the reactivity series? How do displacement reactions help us compare the reactivity of metals?
question_hinglish: Reactivity series kya hai? Displacement reactions metals ki reactivity compare karne mein kaise madad karti hain?
answer_english: The reactivity (activity) series is a list of metals arranged in decreasing order of reactivity: K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Pb > [H] > Cu > Hg > Ag > Au. Displacement reactions give clear evidence: if metal A displaces metal B from its salt solution, A is more reactive than B. For example, an iron nail in copper sulphate solution displaces copper, but a copper wire in iron sulphate does not react, so iron is more reactive than copper.
answer_hinglish: Reactivity (activity) series metals ki reactivity ke ghatte kram mein bani soochi hai: K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Pb > [H] > Cu > Hg > Ag > Au. Displacement reactions saaf saboot deti hain: agar metal A metal B ko uske salt solution se hata de, toh A, B se zyada reactive hai. Jaise copper sulphate solution mein iron ki keel copper ko hata deti hai, par iron sulphate mein copper ka taar react nahi karta, isliye iron copper se zyada reactive hai.
ncert_context: Reactive metals can displace less reactive metals from their compounds in solution or molten form. Displacement reactions give better evidence about the reactivity of metals. It is simple and easy if metal A displaces metal B from its solution, it is more reactive than B. Metal A + Salt solution of B → Salt solution of A + Metal B. subject: Chemistry
question_english: Metals A, B, C and D were added to solutions: A displaces copper from copper(II) sulphate; B displaces iron from iron(II) sulphate but not zinc from zinc sulphate; C displaces silver from silver nitrate only; D reacts with none. Which is most reactive, what happens when B is added to copper(II) sulphate, and what is the order of reactivity?
question_hinglish: Metals A, B, C aur D ko solutions mein daala gaya: A copper(II) sulphate se copper hatata hai; B iron(II) sulphate se iron hatata hai par zinc sulphate se zinc nahi; C sirf silver nitrate se silver hatata hai; D kisi se react nahi karta. Sabse reactive kaun hai, B ko copper(II) sulphate mein daalne pe kya hoga, aur reactivity ka kram kya hai?
answer_english:
(i) B is the most reactive, since it displaces iron, which is above copper in the series.
(ii) B will displace copper from copper(II) sulphate: the blue colour fades and reddish-brown copper deposits.
(iii) A displaces copper but not iron, C displaces only silver, and D displaces nothing. Order of decreasing reactivity: B > A > C > D.
answer_hinglish:
(i) B sabse reactive hai, kyunki woh iron ko hatata hai, jo series mein copper se upar hai.
(ii) B copper(II) sulphate se copper ko hata dega: neela rang feeka padega aur laal-bhoora copper jamega.
(iii) A copper hatata hai par iron nahi, C sirf silver hatata hai, aur D kuch nahi hatata. Ghatti reactivity ka kram: B > A > C > D.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: What would you observe when zinc is added to iron(II) sulphate solution? Write the equation. Also write the reaction of iron with dilute sulphuric acid.
question_hinglish: Iron(II) sulphate solution mein zinc daalne pe kya dikhega? Equation likho. Iron ki dilute sulphuric acid ke saath reaction bhi likho.
answer_english:
Zinc is more reactive than iron, so it displaces iron: the pale green colour of iron(II) sulphate fades and iron deposits.
Zn(s) + FeSO₄(aq) → ZnSO₄(aq) + Fe(s)
Iron with dilute sulphuric acid gives iron(II) sulphate and hydrogen gas:
Fe(s) + H₂SO₄(aq) → FeSO₄(aq) + H₂(g)
answer_hinglish:
Zinc iron se zyada reactive hai, isliye woh iron ko hata deta hai: iron(II) sulphate ka halka hara rang feeka padta hai aur iron jam jaata hai.

Iron dilute sulphuric acid ke saath iron(II) sulphate aur hydrogen gas deta hai:
Fe(s) + H₂SO₄(aq) → FeSO₄(aq) + H₂(g)

question_english: Which pair will give a displacement reaction? (a) NaCl solution and copper (b) MgCl₂ solution and aluminium (c) FeSO₄ solution and silver (d) AgNO₃ solution and copper
question_hinglish: Kaun sa jodaa displacement reaction dega? (a) NaCl solution aur copper (b) MgCl₂ solution aur aluminium (c) FeSO₄ solution aur silver (d) AgNO₃ solution aur copper

subject: Chemistry
question_english: Zinc oxide, magnesium oxide and copper oxide are each heated with zinc, magnesium and copper metals. In which cases will displacement occur?
question_hinglish: Zinc oxide, magnesium oxide aur copper oxide ko zinc, magnesium aur copper metals ke saath garam kiya jaata hai. Kin cases mein displacement hoga?
answer_english:
A metal displaces another from its oxide only if it is more reactive (Mg > Zn > Cu).
Magnesium with zinc oxide: displaces zinc.
Magnesium with copper oxide: displaces copper.
Zinc with copper oxide: displaces copper.
No reaction for: zinc or copper with magnesium oxide, copper with zinc oxide, or any metal with its own oxide.
answer_hinglish:
Metal doosre ko uske oxide se tabhi hatata hai jab woh zyada reactive ho (Mg > Zn > Cu).
Magnesium aur zinc oxide: zinc hatata hai.
Magnesium aur copper oxide: copper hatata hai.
Zinc aur copper oxide: copper hatata hai.
Reaction nahi: zinc ya copper ke saath magnesium oxide, copper ke saath zinc oxide, ya kisi metal ke saath uska apna oxide.

question_english: Show the formation of Na₂O and MgO by transfer of electrons. What ions are present in these compounds?
question_hinglish: Electrons ke transfer se Na₂O aur MgO ka banna dikhao. In compounds mein kaun se ions hain?
answer_english:
Na₂O: each sodium (2, 8, 1) loses one electron to form Na⁺; oxygen (2, 6) gains two electrons, one from each of two sodium atoms, to form O²⁻. So 2Na → 2Na⁺ + 2e⁻ and O + 2e⁻ → O²⁻, giving Na₂O with ions Na⁺ and O²⁻.
MgO: magnesium (2, 8, 2) loses two electrons to form Mg²⁺, and oxygen gains them to form O²⁻, giving MgO with ions Mg²⁺ and O²⁻.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: List the general properties of ionic compounds.
question_hinglish: Ionic compounds ke saamaanya gun batao.
answer_english:
1. Physical nature: solid and somewhat hard due to strong attraction between ions, and generally brittle, breaking under pressure.
2. High melting and boiling points, since much energy is needed to break the strong inter-ionic attraction.
3. Generally soluble in water but insoluble in kerosene and petrol.
4. They conduct electricity in solution and in the molten state, where ions move freely, but not as solids, where ions are held rigidly.
answer_hinglish:
1. Bhautik roop: ions ke beech mazboot aakarshan ki wajah se solid aur kuch kathor, aur aam taur pe bhangur, dabaav se toot jaate hain.
2. Oonche melting aur boiling points, kyunki mazboot inter-ionic aakarshan todne mein bahut urja lagti hai.
3. Aam taur pe paani mein ghulte hain par kerosene aur petrol mein nahi.
4. Solution aur pighli avastha mein bijli conduct karte hain, jahan ions aazaad ghoomte hain, par solid mein nahi, jahan ions kas kar bandhe hote hain.
ncert_context: General properties for ionic compounds— (i) Physical nature: Ionic compounds are solids and are somewhat hard because of the strong force of attraction between the positive and negative ions. These compounds are generally brittle and break into pieces when pressure is applied. (ii) Melting and Boiling points: Ionic compounds have high melting and boiling points. This is because a considerable amount of energy is required to break the strong inter-ionic attraction. (iii) Solubility: Electrovalent compounds are generally soluble in water and insoluble in solvents such as kerosene, petrol, etc. (iv) Conduction of Electricity: A solution of an ionic compound in water contains ions, which move to the opposite electrodes when electricity is passed. Ionic compounds in the solid state do not conduct electricity because movement of ions in the solid is not possible due to their rigid structure. But ionic compounds conduct electricity in the molten state, since the electrostatic forces of attraction are overcome due to the heat.

answer_english: Minerals are elements or compounds that occur naturally in the earth's crust; an ore is a mineral with a high enough percentage of a metal that the metal can be profitably extracted. Metals of low reactivity, like gold, silver, platinum and copper, are often found free. Highly reactive metals (K, Na, Ca, Mg, Al) never occur free. Moderately reactive metals (Zn, Fe, Pb) occur mainly as oxides, sulphides or carbonates.

Madhyam reactive metals (Zn, Fe, Pb) mukhya roop se oxides, sulphides ya carbonates ke roop mein milte hain.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: How are metals low in the activity series, like mercury and copper, extracted from their ores?
question_hinglish: Activity series mein neeche wale metals, jaise mercury aur copper, ores se kaise nikaale jaate hain?
answer_english:
Their oxides can be reduced to metal by heating alone.
Mercury: cinnabar (HgS) is heated in air to form mercuric oxide, which is reduced to mercury on further heating:
2HgS + 3O₂ → 2HgO + 2SO₂; 2HgO → 2Hg + O₂
Copper: Cu₂S is heated in air:
2Cu₂S + 3O₂ → 2Cu₂O + 2SO₂; 2Cu₂O + Cu₂S → 6Cu + SO₂
answer_hinglish:
Inke oxides sirf garam karke metal mein reduce ho jaate hain.
Mercury: cinnabar (HgS) ko hawa mein garam karne pe mercuric oxide banta hai, jo aur garam karne pe mercury mein reduce hota hai:
2HgS + 3O₂ → 2HgO + 2SO₂; 2HgO → 2Hg + O₂
Copper: Cu₂S ko hawa mein garam kiya jaata hai:
2Cu₂S + 3O₂ → 2Cu₂O + 2SO₂; 2Cu₂O + Cu₂S → 6Cu + SO₂
ncert_context: Metals low in the activity series are very unreactive. The oxides of these metals can be reduced to metals by heating alone. For example, cinnabar (HgS) is an ore of mercury. When it is heated in air, it is first converted into mercuric oxide (HgO). Mercuric oxide is then reduced to mercury on further heating. 2HgS(s) + 3O₂(g) → 2HgO(s) + 2SO₂(g) (heat); 2HgO(s) → 2Hg(l) + O₂(g) (heat). Similarly, copper which is found as Cu₂S in nature can be obtained from its ore by just heating in air. 2Cu₂S + 3O₂(g) → 2Cu₂O(s) + 2SO₂(g); 2Cu₂O + Cu₂S → 6Cu(s) + SO₂(g).

subject: Chemistry
question_english: What is the difference between roasting and calcination? Explain with zinc ores.
question_hinglish: Roasting aur calcination mein kya fark hai? Zinc ores se samjhao.
answer_english:
Both convert ores into oxides before reduction, since it is easier to get a metal from its oxide.
Roasting: sulphide ores are heated strongly in excess air: 2ZnS + 3O₂ → 2ZnO + 2SO₂.
Calcination: carbonate ores are heated strongly in limited air: ZnCO₃ → ZnO + CO₂.
The zinc oxide is then reduced with carbon: ZnO + C → Zn + CO.
answer_hinglish:
Dono reduction se pehle ores ko oxides mein badalte hain, kyunki oxide se metal nikaalna aasaan hai.
Roasting: sulphide ores ko zyada hawa mein tez garam kiya jaata hai: 2ZnS + 3O₂ → 2ZnO + 2SO₂.
Calcination: carbonate ores ko kam hawa mein tez garam kiya jaata hai: ZnCO₃ → ZnO + CO₂.
Phir zinc oxide ko carbon se reduce karte hain: ZnO + C → Zn + CO.
ncert_context: The metals in the middle of the activity series such as iron, zinc, lead, copper, are moderately reactive. These are usually present as sulphides or carbonates in nature. It is easier to obtain a metal from its oxide, as compared to its sulphides and carbonates. Therefore, prior to reduction, the metal sulphides and carbonates must be converted into metal oxides. The sulphide ores are converted into oxides by heating strongly in the presence of excess air. This process is known as roasting. The carbonate ores are changed into oxides by heating strongly in limited air. This process is known as calcination. Roasting: 2ZnS(s) + 3O₂(g) → 2ZnO(s) + 2SO₂(g). Calcination: ZnCO₃(s) → ZnO(s) + CO₂(g). When zinc oxide is heated with carbon, it is reduced to metallic zinc. ZnO(s) + C(s) → Zn(s) + CO(g).

subject: Chemistry
question_english: What is the thermit reaction, and what is it used for?
question_hinglish: Thermit reaction kya hai, aur iska kya upyog hai?
answer_english:
In the thermit reaction, aluminium, a highly reactive metal, displaces iron from iron(III) oxide:
Fe₂O₃(s) + 2Al(s) → 2Fe(l) + Al₂O₃(s) + Heat
It is so exothermic that iron is produced in the molten state. It is used to join railway tracks and cracked machine parts. Here Fe₂O₃ is reduced and aluminium is oxidised.
answer_hinglish:
Thermit reaction mein bahut reactive metal aluminium iron(III) oxide se iron ko hata deta hai:
Fe₂O₃(s) + 2Al(s) → 2Fe(l) + Al₂O₃(s) + Heat
Yeh itni exothermic hai ki iron pighli avastha mein banta hai. Iska use railway patriyon aur toote machine ke hisson ko jodne mein hota hai. Isme Fe₂O₃ reduce hota hai aur aluminium oxidise hota hai.
ncert_context: Besides using carbon (coke) to reduce metal oxides to metals, sometimes displacement reactions can also be used. The highly reactive metals such as sodium, calcium, aluminium, etc., are used as reducing agents because they can displace metals of lower reactivity from their compounds. When manganese dioxide is heated with aluminium powder: 3MnO₂(s) + 4Al(s) → 3Mn(l) + 2Al₂O₃(s) + Heat. These displacement reactions are highly exothermic. The amount of heat evolved is so large that the metals are produced in the molten state. In fact, the reaction of iron(III) oxide (Fe₂O₃) with aluminium is used to join railway tracks or cracked machine parts. This reaction is known as the thermit reaction. Fe₂O₃(s) + 2Al(s) → 2Fe(l) + Al₂O₃(s) + Heat.

question_hinglish: 3MnO₂ + 4Al → 3Mn + 2Al₂O₃ + Heat mein kaun oxidise hota hai aur kaun reduce?

subject: Chemistry
question_english: Why are carbonate and sulphide ores usually converted into oxides during extraction? What is gangue?
question_hinglish: Extraction mein carbonate aur sulphide ores ko aam taur pe oxides mein kyun badla jaata hai? Gangue kya hai?
answer_english: It is easier to obtain a metal from its oxide than from its sulphide or carbonate, so these ores are first converted into oxides by roasting or calcination and then reduced. Gangue is the impurities, such as soil and sand, mixed with ores mined from the earth; it must be removed before extracting the metal, using methods based on differences in physical or chemical properties.
answer_hinglish: Sulphide ya carbonate ki tulna mein oxide se metal nikaalna aasaan hai, isliye in ores ko pehle roasting ya calcination se oxides mein badal kar reduce kiya jaata hai. Gangue dharti se khode gaye ores mein mili mitti aur ret jaisi ashuddhiyan hain; metal nikaalne se pehle inhe physical ya chemical gunon ke antar pe aadhaarit tareekon se hataana padta hai.
ncert_context: Ores mined from the earth are usually contaminated with large amounts of impurities such as soil, sand, etc., called gangue. The impurities must be removed from the ore prior to the extraction of the metal. The processes used for removing the gangue from the ore are based on the differences between the physical or chemical properties of the gangue and the ore. It is easier to obtain a metal from its oxide, as compared to its sulphides and carbonates. Therefore, prior to reduction, the metal sulphides and carbonates must be converted into metal oxides.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: Describe electrolytic refining of a metal. What is taken as the anode, cathode and electrolyte, and what is anode mud?
question_hinglish: Metal ki electrolytic refining ka varnan karo. Anode, cathode aur electrolyte kya lete hain, aur anode mud kya hai?
answer_english: In electrolytic refining, the impure metal is made the anode, a thin strip of pure metal is the cathode, and a solution of the metal's salt is the electrolyte. On passing current, pure metal from the anode dissolves into the electrolyte, and an equal amount of pure metal is deposited on the cathode. Soluble impurities go into the solution, and insoluble impurities settle below the anode as anode mud. Copper, zinc, tin, nickel, silver and gold are refined this way.
answer_hinglish: Electrolytic refining mein ashuddh metal ko anode, shuddh metal ki patli patti ko cathode, aur us metal ke salt ke solution ko electrolyte banaate hain. Current guzaarne pe anode se shuddh metal electrolyte mein ghulta hai, aur utna hi shuddh metal cathode pe jamta hai. Ghulne wali ashuddhiyan solution mein jaati hain, aur na ghulne wali anode ke neeche anode mud ke roop mein baith jaati hain. Copper, zinc, tin, nickel, silver aur gold aise hi refine hote hain.
ncert_context: The metals produced by various reduction processes are not very pure. The most widely used method for refining impure metals is electrolytic refining. Many metals, such as copper, zinc, tin, nickel, silver, gold, etc., are refined electrolytically. In this process, the impure metal is made the anode and a thin strip of pure metal is made the cathode. A solution of the metal salt is used as an electrolyte. On passing the current through the electrolyte, the pure metal from the anode dissolves into the electrolyte. An equivalent amount of pure metal from the electrolyte is deposited on the cathode. The soluble impurities go into the solution, whereas, the insoluble impurities settle down at the bottom of the anode and are known as anode mud.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: What are the conditions for rusting of iron? Explain the experiment with three test tubes.
question_hinglish: Iron mein jang lagne ki shartein kya hain? Teen test tubes wala experiment samjhao.
answer_english: Iron rusts only when exposed to both air and water. In tube A, nails in ordinary water with air rust. In tube B, nails in boiled distilled water covered with an oil layer (so no air dissolves) do not rust. In tube C, nails in dry air with anhydrous calcium chloride absorbing moisture do not rust. So both air (oxygen) and moisture are needed for rusting.
answer_hinglish: Iron mein jang tabhi lagta hai jab woh hawa aur paani dono ke sampark mein ho. Tube A mein hawa ke saath saadharan paani mein keelein jang kha jaati hain. Tube B mein tel ki parat se dhake ubale distilled water (jisme hawa nahi ghulti) mein keelein jang nahi khaati. Tube C mein nami soakhne wale anhydrous calcium chloride ke saath sukhi hawa mein keelein jang nahi khaati. Yaani jang ke liye hawa (oxygen) aur nami dono chahiye.
ncert_context: Take three test tubes and place clean iron nails in each of them. Label these test tubes A, B and C. Pour some water in test tube A and cork it. Pour boiled distilled water in test tube B, add about 1 mL of oil and cork it. The oil will float on water and prevent the air from dissolving in the water. Put some anhydrous calcium chloride in test tube C and cork it. Anhydrous calcium chloride will absorb the moisture, if any, from the air. Leave these test tubes for a few days and then observe. You will observe that iron nails rust in test tube A, but they do not rust in test tubes B and C. In the test tube A, the nails are exposed to both air and water. In the test tube B, the nails are exposed to only water, and the nails in test tube C are exposed to dry air.

question_english: Give examples of corrosion of silver, copper and iron.
question_hinglish: Silver, copper aur iron ke corrosion ke examples do.
answer_english: Silver articles turn black because silver reacts with sulphur in the air to form a coating of silver sulphide. Copper slowly loses its shiny brown surface and gains a green coat of basic copper carbonate by reacting with moist carbon dioxide in the air. Iron exposed to moist air for a long time gets a coating of a brown flaky substance called rust.
answer_hinglish: Silver ki cheezein kaali pad jaati hain kyunki silver hawa ke sulphur se react karke silver sulphide ki parat banata hai. Copper hawa ki nam carbon dioxide se react karke dheere-dheere apni chamakdaar bhoori satah kho deta hai aur uspe basic copper carbonate ki hari parat chadh jaati hai. Lambe samay tak nam hawa mein rakhe iron pe rust naam ka bhoora, papdi jaisa padaarth chadh jaata hai.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: List the methods to prevent rusting of iron. What is galvanisation?
question_hinglish: Iron mein jang rokne ke tareeke batao. Galvanisation kya hai?
answer_english: Rusting can be prevented by painting, oiling, greasing, galvanising, chrome plating, anodising or making alloys. Galvanisation protects steel and iron by coating them with a thin layer of zinc; the galvanised article stays protected against rusting even if the zinc coating is broken, because zinc is more reactive than iron.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: What is an alloy? Why is pure iron not used, and how does alloying improve it?
question_hinglish: Alloy kya hai? Shuddh iron kyun use nahi hota, aur alloy banane se woh kaise behtar hota hai?
answer_english: An alloy is a homogeneous mixture of two or more metals, or a metal and a non-metal, made by melting the main metal and dissolving the others in definite proportions, then cooling. Pure iron is very soft and stretches easily when hot, so it is never used pure. With a small amount of carbon (about 0.05%), it becomes hard and strong; with nickel and chromium, it forms stainless steel, which is hard and does not rust.
answer_hinglish: Alloy do ya zyada metals, ya ek metal aur ek non-metal, ka homogeneous mixture hai, jo mukhya metal ko pighla kar baaki ko tay anupaat mein gholkar aur phir thanda karke banta hai. Shuddh iron bahut naram hota hai aur garam hone pe aasaani se khinch jaata hai, isliye shuddh roop mein use nahi hota. Thoda carbon (lagbhag 0.05%) milaane se woh kathor aur mazboot ho jaata hai; nickel aur chromium milaane se stainless steel banta hai, jo kathor hai aur jang nahi khaata.
ncert_context: Alloying is a very good method of improving the properties of a metal. Iron is the most widely used metal. But it is never used in its pure state. This is because pure iron is very soft and stretches easily when hot. But, if it is mixed with a small amount of carbon (about 0.05 %), it becomes hard and strong. When iron is mixed with nickel and chromium, we get stainless steel, which is hard and does not rust. An alloy is a homogeneous mixture of two or more metals, or a metal and a nonmetal. It is prepared by first melting the primary metal, and then, dissolving the other elements in it in definite proportions. It is then cooled to room temperature.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: 22 carat gold is 22 parts of pure gold alloyed with 2 parts of copper or silver. What percentage of 22 carat gold is pure gold? How much pure gold is in a 12 g, 22 carat ornament?
question_hinglish: 22 carat gold mein 22 hisse shuddh gold aur 2 hisse copper ya silver hota hai. 22 carat gold mein kitne percent shuddh gold hai? 12 g ke 22 carat gehne mein kitna shuddh gold hai?
answer_english:
Total parts = 22 + 2 = 24 (pure gold is 24 carat)
Percentage of gold = (22 ÷ 24) × 100 ≈ 91.7%
Pure gold in 12 g = (22 ÷ 24) × 12 g = 11 g
Pure gold is too soft, so it is alloyed with copper or silver to make jewellery hard.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: How do the properties of alloys like brass, bronze and solder differ from pure metals? What is an amalgam?
question_hinglish: Brass, bronze aur solder jaise alloys ke gun shuddh metals se kaise alag hain? Amalgam kya hai?
answer_english: Alloys have lower electrical conductivity and lower melting points than pure metals. Brass (copper and zinc) and bronze (copper and tin) are not good conductors of electricity, while copper is used for electrical circuits. Solder (lead and tin) has a low melting point and is used to weld electrical wires. An alloy in which one metal is mercury is called an amalgam.
answer_hinglish: Alloys ki electrical conductivity aur melting point shuddh metals se kam hote hain. Brass (copper aur zinc) aur bronze (copper aur tin) bijli ke achhe conductor nahi hain, jabki copper bijli ke circuits mein use hota hai. Solder (lead aur tin) ka melting point kam hai aur woh bijli ke taar jodne mein use hota hai. Jis alloy mein ek metal mercury ho, use amalgam kehte hain.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: Differentiate between metals and non-metals on the basis of their chemical properties.
question_hinglish: Chemical gunon ke aadhaar pe metals aur non-metals mein fark batao.
answer_english: Metals form positive ions by losing electrons, while non-metals form negative ions by gaining electrons when reacting with metals. Metals form basic oxides (some, like Al₂O₃ and ZnO, are amphoteric), while non-metals form acidic or neutral oxides. Metals above hydrogen displace hydrogen from dilute acids, while non-metals do not. Non-metals react with hydrogen to form hydrides.
answer_hinglish: Metals electrons khokar positive ions banate hain, jabki non-metals metals se react karte waqt electrons lekar negative ions banate hain. Metals basic oxides banate hain (Al₂O₃ aur ZnO jaise kuch amphoteric hain), jabki non-metals acidic ya neutral oxides banate hain. Hydrogen se upar ke metals dilute acids se hydrogen hatate hain, jabki non-metals nahi. Non-metals hydrogen ke saath react karke hydrides banate hain.
ncert_context: Metals can form positive ions by losing electrons to non-metals. Metals combine with oxygen to form basic oxides. Aluminium oxide and zinc oxide show the properties of both basic as well as acidic oxides; these are amphoteric oxides. Metals above hydrogen in the Activity series can displace hydrogen from dilute acids. Non-metals form negatively charged ions by gaining electrons when reacting with metals. Non-metals form oxides which are either acidic or neutral. Non-metals do not displace hydrogen from dilute acids. They react with hydrogen to form hydrides.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: Sulphur powder is heated and the gas evolved is collected. What is the action of the gas on dry and on moist litmus paper? Write the equation.
question_hinglish: Sulphur powder garam karke nikli gas ikatthi ki jaati hai. Gas ka sukhe aur geele litmus paper pe kya asar hoga? Equation likho.
answer_english:
Sulphur burns to form sulphur dioxide: S(s) + O₂(g) → SO₂(g).
(i) Dry litmus paper: no change, because the gas cannot form an acid without water.
(ii) Moist blue litmus paper: turns red, because SO₂ dissolves in the water to form an acidic solution; non-metallic oxides are acidic.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: Give reasons: (a) platinum, gold and silver are used for jewellery (b) tarnished copper vessels are cleaned with lemon or tamarind juice (c) copper, not steel, is used for hot water tanks.
question_hinglish: Kaaran do: (a) platinum, gold aur silver gehnon mein kyun use hote hain (b) kaale pade copper ke bartan nimbu ya imli se kyun saaf kiye jaate hain (c) garam paani ke tank copper ke kyun bante hain, steel ke nahi.
answer_english:
(a) They are very unreactive and do not react with oxygen or water, so they stay shiny; gold and silver are also very malleable and ductile.
(b) The green tarnish on copper is basic copper carbonate; the acids in lemon (citric acid) and tamarind (tartaric acid) neutralise it and dissolve it, restoring the shine.
(c) Copper does not react with water at all, while iron in steel reacts with steam and rusts in moist air, so copper lasts longer and conducts heat well.
answer_hinglish:
(a) Yeh bahut kam reactive hain aur oxygen ya paani se react nahi karte, isliye chamakdaar rehte hain; gold aur silver bahut malleable aur ductile bhi hain.

(c) Copper paani se bilkul react nahi karta, jabki steel ka iron bhaap se react karta hai aur nam hawa mein jang khaata hai, isliye copper zyada tikta hai aur garmi bhi achhe se conduct karta hai.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: Why does carbon form compounds by sharing electrons rather than by gaining or losing them?
question_hinglish: Carbon electrons lene ya dene ki jagah share karke compounds kyun banata hai?
answer_english: Carbon (2, 4) has four valence electrons and needs four more or four fewer to attain noble gas configuration. Gaining four to form C⁴⁻ is difficult because a nucleus with six protons cannot easily hold ten electrons. Losing four to form C⁴⁺ needs a large amount of energy, leaving six protons holding just two electrons. So carbon shares its valence electrons with other carbon atoms or other elements, forming covalent bonds.
answer_hinglish: Carbon (2, 4) mein chaar valence electrons hain aur noble gas configuration ke liye use chaar aur lene ya chaar dene padenge. Chaar lekar C⁴⁻ banana mushkil hai, kyunki chhe protons wala nucleus das electrons ko aasaani se nahi sambhaal sakta. Chaar dekar C⁴⁺ banane mein bahut urja lagti hai, aur chhe protons sirf do electrons ko pakde rehte. Isliye carbon apne valence electrons doosre carbon atoms ya elements ke saath share karke covalent bonds banata hai.
ncert_context: The atomic number of carbon is 6. Carbon has four electrons in its outermost shell and needs to gain or lose four electrons to attain noble gas configuration. If it were to gain or lose electrons – (i) It could gain four electrons forming C⁴⁻ anion. But it would be difficult for the nucleus with six protons to hold on to ten electrons, that is, four extra electrons. (ii) It could lose four electrons forming C⁴⁺ cation. But it would require a large amount of energy to remove four electrons leaving behind a carbon cation with six protons in its nucleus holding on to just two electrons. Carbon overcomes this problem by sharing its valence electrons with other atoms of carbon or with atoms of other elements.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: Explain single, double and triple covalent bonds with the examples of hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen molecules.
question_hinglish: Hydrogen, oxygen aur nitrogen molecules ke examples se single, double aur triple covalent bonds samjhao.
answer_english:
Single bond: two hydrogen atoms share one pair of electrons (one from each), so each attains helium's configuration: H—H.
Double bond: each oxygen atom (2, 6) needs two electrons, so two oxygen atoms share two pairs: O=O.
Triple bond: each nitrogen atom (2, 5) contributes three electrons, giving three shared pairs: N≡N.
answer_hinglish:
Single bond: do hydrogen atoms electrons ka ek pair (har ek se ek) share karte hain, jisse dono helium jaisi configuration paate hain: H—H.
Double bond: har oxygen atom (2, 6) ko do electrons chahiye, isliye do oxygen atoms do pairs share karte hain: O=O.
Triple bond: har nitrogen atom (2, 5) teen electrons deta hai, jisse teen shared pairs bante hain: N≡N.
ncert_context: Hydrogen has one electron in its K shell and requires one more electron to fill the K shell. So two hydrogen atoms share their electrons to form a molecule of hydrogen, H₂. The shared pair of electrons is said to constitute a single covalent bond between the two hydrogen atoms. An atom of oxygen has six electrons in its L shell and it requires two more electrons to complete its octet. So each atom of oxygen shares two electrons with another atom of oxygen. The two electrons contributed by each oxygen atom give rise to two shared pairs of electrons. This is said to constitute a double bond between the two atoms. Nitrogen has the atomic number 7. In order to attain an octet, each nitrogen atom in a molecule of nitrogen contributes three electrons giving rise to three shared pairs of electrons. This is said to constitute a triple bond between the two atoms.

question_english: The melting and boiling points (K) of some carbon compounds are: acetic acid 290 and 391, chloroform 209 and 334, ethanol 156 and 351, methane 90 and 111. How do these compare with ionic compounds like NaCl (1074 K and 1686 K), and what does this show?
question_hinglish: Kuch carbon compounds ke melting aur boiling points (K) hain: acetic acid 290 aur 391, chloroform 209 aur 334, ethanol 156 aur 351, methane 90 aur 111. Inki tulna NaCl (1074 K aur 1686 K) jaise ionic compounds se kaise hai, aur isse kya pata chalta hai?
answer_english:
Highest melting point among them: acetic acid, 290 K; NaCl melts at 1074 K, about 3.7 times higher (1074 ÷ 290 ≈ 3.7).
Highest boiling point: acetic acid, 391 K, versus 1686 K for NaCl.
Carbon compounds have much lower melting and boiling points, showing that the forces between their molecules are weak, unlike the strong attraction between ions in ionic compounds.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: How do diamond and graphite differ in structure and properties? What are fullerenes?
question_hinglish: Diamond aur graphite ki banaavat aur gunon mein kya fark hai? Fullerenes kya hain?
answer_english: In diamond, each carbon atom is bonded to four others in a rigid three-dimensional structure, making it the hardest substance known. In graphite, each carbon is bonded to three others in a plane, forming hexagonal arrays stacked in layers, with one double bond; graphite is smooth, slippery and a very good conductor of electricity. Their chemical properties are the same. Fullerenes are another class of allotropes; the first, C-60, has carbon atoms arranged like a football and is named after architect Buckminster Fuller.
answer_hinglish: Diamond mein har carbon atom chaar doosre atoms se judkar ek kadi teen-dimensional banaavat banata hai, isliye yeh sabse kathor padaarth hai. Graphite mein har carbon ek hi samtal mein teen doosron se juda hota hai, jisse hexagonal jaal bante hain jo parton mein jame hote hain, aur ek double bond hota hai; graphite chikna, phisalne wala aur bijli ka bahut achha conductor hai. Inke chemical gun same hain. Fullerenes allotropes ki ek aur shreni hai; pehla, C-60, football jaisa aakaar rakhta hai aur architect Buckminster Fuller ke naam pe hai.
ncert_context: The element carbon occurs in different forms in nature with widely varying physical properties. Both diamond and graphite are formed by carbon atoms, the difference lies in the manner in which the carbon atoms are bonded to one another. In diamond, each carbon atom is bonded to four other carbon atoms forming a rigid three-dimensional structure. In graphite, each carbon atom is bonded to three other carbon atoms in the same plane giving a hexagonal array. One of these bonds is a double-bond. Graphite structure is formed by the hexagonal arrays being placed in layers one above the other. These two different structures result in diamond and graphite having very different physical properties even though their chemical properties are the same. Diamond is the hardest substance known while graphite is smooth and slippery. Graphite is also a very good conductor of electricity. Fullerenes form another class of carbon allotropes. The first one to be identified was C-60 which has carbon atoms arranged in the shape of a football. Since this looked like the geodesic dome designed by the US architect Buckminster Fuller, the molecule was named fullerene.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: What two properties of carbon lead to the huge number of carbon compounds?
question_hinglish: Carbon ke kaun se do gun itne saare carbon compounds banne ka kaaran hain?
answer_english:
1. Catenation: carbon can bond with other carbon atoms to form large molecules with long chains, branched chains or rings, linked by single, double or triple bonds; the C–C bond is very strong and stable. No other element shows catenation to this extent; silicon forms chains of only seven or eight atoms, which are very reactive.
2. Tetravalency: with a valency of four, carbon can bond with four other atoms, such as oxygen, hydrogen, nitrogen, sulphur or chlorine. Its small size lets its nucleus hold shared electrons strongly, making these bonds very stable.
answer_hinglish:
1.
