Koi aur element itna catenation nahi dikhata; silicon sirf saat-aath atoms ki chains banata hai, jo bahut reactive hain.
2. Tetravalency: chaar valency ke saath carbon oxygen, hydrogen, nitrogen, sulphur ya chlorine jaise chaar doosre atoms se jud sakta hai. Chhote aakaar ki wajah se uska nucleus share kiye electrons ko mazbooti se pakadta hai, isliye yeh bonds bahut sthir hote hain.
ncert_context: The nature of the covalent bond enables carbon to form a large number of compounds. (i) Carbon has the unique ability to form bonds with other atoms of carbon, giving rise to large molecules. This property is called catenation. These compounds may have long chains of carbon, branched chains of carbon or even carbon atoms arranged in rings. Carbon atoms may be linked by single, double or triple bonds. No other element exhibits the property of catenation to the extent seen in carbon compounds. Silicon forms compounds with hydrogen which have chains of upto seven or eight atoms, but these compounds are very reactive. The carbon-carbon bond is very strong and hence stable. (ii) Since carbon has a valency of four, it is capable of bonding with four other atoms of carbon or atoms of some other mono-valent element. Compounds of carbon are formed with oxygen, hydrogen, nitrogen, sulphur, chlorine and many other elements. One reason for the formation of strong bonds by carbon is its small size. This enables the nucleus to hold on to the shared pairs of electrons strongly.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: Why were carbon compounds called organic compounds, and how was the vital force theory disproved?
question_hinglish: Carbon compounds ko organic compounds kyun kaha gaya, aur vital force theory kaise galat saabit hui?
answer_english: Carbon compounds were first extracted from natural substances, and it was thought they could only be formed within living systems, needing a 'vital force'. Friedrich Wöhler disproved this in 1828 by preparing urea from ammonium cyanate. Carbon compounds, except carbides, oxides of carbon, carbonates and hydrogencarbonates, are still studied under organic chemistry.
answer_hinglish: Carbon compounds pehle prakritik padaarthon se nikaale gaye, aur maana gaya ki yeh sirf jeevit sharir mein ban sakte hain, jiske liye 'vital force' chahiye. Friedrich Wöhler ne 1828 mein ammonium cyanate se urea banakar ise galat saabit kiya. subject: Chemistry
question_english: How many covalent bonds are there in ethane, C₂H₆?
question_hinglish: Ethane, C₂H₆, mein kitne covalent bonds hain?
answer_english:
Ethane has two carbon atoms joined by one C–C single bond, and each carbon is bonded to three hydrogen atoms.
C–C bonds = 1
C–H bonds = 3 + 3 = 6
Total covalent bonds = 1 + 6 = 7

question_english: What are structural isomers? Explain with butane.
question_hinglish: Structural isomers kya hain? Butane se samjhao.
answer_english: Structural isomers are compounds with identical molecular formula but different structures. With four carbon atoms, two skeletons are possible: a straight chain (C—C—C—C) and a branched chain. Filling the remaining valencies with hydrogen gives two different compounds, both with the formula C₄H₁₀, so they are structural isomers of butane.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: What are functional groups and heteroatoms? Name some functional groups.
question_hinglish: Functional groups aur heteroatoms kya hain? Kuch functional groups ke naam batao.
answer_english: When one or more hydrogens in a hydrocarbon chain are replaced by elements such as halogens, oxygen, nitrogen or sulphur, the replacing element is a heteroatom. These heteroatoms and the groups containing them give specific properties to a compound regardless of the carbon chain's length, so they are called functional groups. Examples: halo (—Cl, —Br) in haloalkanes, —OH in alcohols, aldehyde, ketone and carboxylic acid (—COOH) groups.
answer_hinglish: Jab hydrocarbon chain ke ek ya zyada hydrogen halogens, oxygen, nitrogen ya sulphur jaise elements se badle jaate hain, toh badalne wala element heteroatom kehlaata hai. Yeh heteroatoms aur inse bane groups carbon chain ki lambaai se pare compound ko khaas gun dete hain, isliye inhe functional groups kehte hain. Examples: haloalkanes mein halo (—Cl, —Br), alcohols mein —OH, aldehyde, ketone aur carboxylic acid (—COOH) groups.

question_english: What is a homologous series? Explain how physical and chemical properties vary within it.
question_hinglish: Homologous series kya hai? Samjhao ki isme physical aur chemical gun kaise badalte hain.
answer_english: A homologous series is a series of compounds in which the same functional group substitutes for hydrogen in carbon chains of different lengths; successive members differ by a –CH₂– unit. question_english: Find the molecular masses of CH₄, C₂H₆, C₃H₈ and C₄H₁₀ (C = 12 u, H = 1 u). What is the difference between successive members?

question_english: Find the difference in formulae and molecular masses between CH₃OH and C₂H₅OH, C₂H₅OH and C₃H₇OH, and C₃H₇OH and C₄H₉OH. Do they form a homologous series?

answer_english:
Molecular masses (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16): CH₃OH = 32 u, C₂H₅OH = 46 u, C₃H₇OH = 60 u, C₄H₉OH = 74 u.
Each pair differs in formula by –CH₂– and in mass by 14 u (46 − 32, 60 − 46, 74 − 60).
All contain the same –OH group and have similar chemical properties, so arranged by increasing carbon atoms they form a homologous series: methanol, ethanol, propanol, butanol.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: How are carbon compounds named? Give the prefix or suffix for each class of compound with three-carbon examples.
question_hinglish: Carbon compounds ke naam kaise rakhe jaate hain? Har prakaar ke compound ka prefix ya suffix teen-carbon examples ke saath batao.
answer_english:
Count the carbon atoms for the base name (three carbons: propane), then add a prefix or suffix for the functional group; if the suffix starts with a vowel, drop the final 'e' (propane − e + one = propanone).
Haloalkane: prefix chloro/bromo, e.g. chloropropane
Alcohol: suffix -ol, propanol
Aldehyde: suffix -al, propanal
Ketone: suffix -one, propanone
Carboxylic acid: suffix -oic acid, propanoic acid
Alkene: -ene, propene; Alkyne: -yne, propyne
answer_hinglish:
Base naam ke liye carbon atoms gino (teen carbon: propane), phir functional group ke liye prefix ya suffix lagao; agar suffix vowel se shuru ho toh aakhri 'e' hata do (propane − e + one = propanone).
Haloalkane: prefix chloro/bromo, jaise chloropropane
Alcohol: suffix -ol, propanol
Aldehyde: suffix -al, propanal
Ketone: suffix -one, propanone
Carboxylic acid: suffix -oic acid, propanoic acid
Alkene: -ene, propene; Alkyne: -yne, propyne
ncert_context: Naming a carbon compound can be done by the following method – (i) Identify the number of carbon atoms in the compound. A compound having three carbon atoms would have the name propane. (ii) In case a functional group is present, it is indicated in the name with either a prefix or a suffix. (iii) If the suffix of the functional group begins with a vowel a, e, i, o, u, then the name of the carbon chain is modified by deleting the final 'e' and adding the appropriate suffix. For example, a three-carbon chain with a ketone group: Propane – 'e' = propan + 'one' = propanone. (iv) If the carbon chain is unsaturated, then the final 'ane' is substituted by 'ene' or 'yne'. Table 4.4: Halo alkane – prefix chloro, bromo: chloropropane, bromopropane; Alcohol – suffix ol: propanol; Aldehyde – suffix al: propanal; Ketone – suffix one: propanone; Carboxylic acid – suffix oic acid: propanoic acid; Alkenes – suffix ene: propene; Alkynes – suffix yne: propyne.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: Why do saturated hydrocarbons usually burn with a clean flame and unsaturated ones with a sooty flame? What does a blackened cooking vessel indicate?
question_hinglish: Saturated hydrocarbons aam taur pe saaf lau ke saath aur unsaturated kaali dhuen wali lau ke saath kyun jalte hain? Kaala pada khaana banane ka bartan kya batata hai?
answer_english: Saturated hydrocarbons generally burn completely with a clean blue flame, while unsaturated carbon compounds give a yellow flame with lots of black smoke (soot, which is carbon). Limiting the air supply causes incomplete combustion even of saturated hydrocarbons, giving a sooty flame. A gas or kerosene stove has air inlets for a clean blue flame; if the bottoms of vessels get blackened, the air holes are blocked and fuel is being wasted.
answer_hinglish: Saturated hydrocarbons aam taur pe poori tarah jalkar saaf neeli lau dete hain, jabki unsaturated carbon compounds bahut kaale dhuen (kaalikh, jo carbon hai) ke saath peeli lau dete hain. Hawa ki supply kam karne se saturated hydrocarbons bhi adhoore jalte hain aur kaalikh wali lau dete hain. Gas ya kerosene stove mein saaf neeli lau ke liye hawa ke chhed hote hain; agar bartanon ke tale kaale ho rahe hain, toh chhed band hain aur fuel barbaad ho raha hai.
ncert_context: Saturated hydrocarbons will generally give a clean flame while unsaturated carbon compounds will give a yellow flame with lots of black smoke. This results in a sooty deposit on the metal plate. However, limiting the supply of air results in incomplete combustion of even saturated hydrocarbons giving a sooty flame. The gas/kerosene stove used at home has inlets for air so that a sufficiently oxygen-rich mixture is burnt to give a clean blue flame. If you observe the bottoms of cooking vessels getting blackened, it means that the air holes are blocked and fuel is getting wasted. Incomplete combustion gives soot which is carbon.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: Why do some substances burn with a flame and others without? Why is a candle flame yellow?
question_hinglish: Kuch padaarth lau ke saath aur kuch bina lau ke kyun jalte hain? Mombatti ki lau peeli kyun hoti hai?
answer_english: A flame is produced only when gaseous substances burn. When wood or charcoal is lit, its volatile substances vaporise and burn with a flame at first, but coal or charcoal in an angithi may just glow red and give heat without a flame. A luminous flame appears when atoms of the burning gas are heated and glow. The yellow colour of a candle flame comes from glowing particles of unburnt carbon (soot) produced by incomplete combustion.
answer_hinglish: Lau sirf tab banti hai jab gas wale padaarth jalte hain. Lakdi ya koyla jalane pe uske udne wale padaarth bhaap bankar shuru mein lau ke saath jalte hain, par angithi mein koyla kabhi sirf laal chamakta hai aur bina lau garmi deta hai. Chamakdaar lau tab dikhti hai jab jalti gas ke atoms garam hokar chamakte hain. Mombatti ki lau ka peela rang adhoore jalne se bane na jale carbon (kaalikh) ke chamakte kanon se aata hai.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: Why are carbon and its compounds used as fuels for most applications? Why are coal and petroleum called fossil fuels?
question_hinglish: Carbon aur uske compounds zyadatar kaamon mein fuel ki tarah kyun use hote hain? Koyle aur petroleum ko fossil fuels kyun kehte hain?
answer_english: Carbon and most of its compounds burn in oxygen to release a large amount of heat and light, so they make good fuels. Coal formed from the remains of trees, ferns and plants buried and pressed under earth and rock millions of years ago; oil and gas formed from tiny sea plants and animals whose remains were covered by silt and turned into oil and gas by bacteria under high pressure. Since they formed from ancient living remains, they are called fossil fuels.
answer_hinglish: Carbon aur uske zyadatar compounds oxygen mein jalkar bahut garmi aur roshni chhodte hain, isliye achhe fuel hain. Koyla laakhon saal pehle mitti aur chattaanon ke neeche dabe pedon, ferns aur paudhon ke avasheshon se bana; tel aur gas samudra ke chhote paudhon aur jeevon se bane jinke avashesh silt se dhak gaye aur oonche dabaav mein bacteria ne unhe tel aur gas mein badal diya. Kyunki yeh purane jeevon ke avasheshon se bane, inhe fossil fuels kehte hain.
ncert_context: Carbon, in all its allotropic forms, burns in oxygen to give carbon dioxide along with the release of heat and light. Most carbon compounds also release a large amount of heat and light on burning. Coal and petroleum have been formed from biomass which has been subjected to various biological and geological processes. Coal is the remains of trees, ferns, and other plants that lived millions of years ago. These were crushed into the earth, perhaps by earthquakes or volcanic eruptions, pressed down by layers of earth and rock, and slowly decayed into coal. Oil and gas are the remains of millions of tiny plants and animals that lived in the sea. When they died, their bodies sank to the sea bed and were covered by silt. Bacteria attacked the dead remains, turning them into oil and gas under the high pressures. Can you guess why coal and petroleum are called fossil fuels?

subject: Chemistry
question_english: Why is the conversion of ethanol to ethanoic acid an oxidation reaction? What are oxidising agents?
question_hinglish: Ethanol ka ethanoic acid mein badalna oxidation reaction kyun hai? Oxidising agents kya hain?
answer_english: Alkaline potassium permanganate or acidified potassium dichromate converts ethanol to ethanoic acid by adding oxygen to it: CH₃CH₂OH → CH₃COOH. Since oxygen is added, it is an oxidation. Substances that add oxygen to others are oxidising agents. When alkaline KMnO₄ is added drop by drop to warm ethanol, its colour first disappears as it is used up, but persists once excess is added after all the ethanol is oxidised.
answer_hinglish: Alkaline potassium permanganate ya acidified potassium dichromate ethanol mein oxygen jodkar use ethanoic acid mein badalta hai: CH₃CH₂OH → CH₃COOH. Oxygen judti hai, isliye yeh oxidation hai. Doosron mein oxygen jodne wale padaarth oxidising agents kehlaate hain. Garam ethanol mein boond-boond alkaline KMnO₄ daalne pe pehle uska rang khatam ho jaata hai kyunki woh use ho raha hai, par saara ethanol oxidise hone ke baad zyada daalne pe rang bana rehta hai.
ncert_context: Take about 3 mL of ethanol in a test tube and warm it gently in a water bath. Add a 5% solution of alkaline potassium permanganate drop by drop to this solution. Does the colour of potassium permanganate persist when it is added initially? Why does the colour of potassium permanganate not disappear when excess is added? Carbon compounds can be easily oxidised on combustion. In addition to this complete oxidation, we have reactions in which alcohols are converted to carboxylic acids – CH₃CH₂OH → CH₃COOH (alkaline KMnO₄ + heat or acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ + heat). Some substances are capable of adding oxygen to others. These substances are known as oxidising agents. Alkaline potassium permanganate or acidified potassium dichromate are oxidising alcohols to acids, that is, adding oxygen to the starting material.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: What is hydrogenation? What is its industrial application, and why are oils with unsaturated fatty acids recommended?
question_hinglish: Hydrogenation kya hai? Iska industrial upyog kya hai, aur unsaturated fatty acids wale tel kyun suggest kiye jaate hain?
answer_english: Hydrogenation is an addition reaction in which unsaturated hydrocarbons add hydrogen in the presence of a catalyst such as nickel or palladium to give saturated hydrocarbons. It is used industrially to hydrogenate vegetable oils with a nickel catalyst. Vegetable oils have long unsaturated carbon chains, while animal fats have saturated chains; saturated fatty acids are said to be harmful for health, so oils with unsaturated fatty acids should be chosen for cooking.
answer_hinglish: Hydrogenation ek addition reaction hai jisme unsaturated hydrocarbons nickel ya palladium jaise catalyst ki maujoodgi mein hydrogen jodkar saturated hydrocarbons bante hain. Industry mein iska use nickel catalyst se vanaspati telon ke hydrogenation mein hota hai. Vanaspati telon mein lambi unsaturated carbon chains hoti hain, jabki jaanwaron ki charbi mein saturated chains; saturated fatty acids sehat ke liye nuksaandeh maane jaate hain, isliye khaana banane ke liye unsaturated fatty acids wale tel chunne chahiye.
ncert_context: Unsaturated hydrocarbons add hydrogen in the presence of catalysts such as palladium or nickel to give saturated hydrocarbons. Catalysts are substances that cause a reaction to occur or proceed at a different rate without the reaction itself being affected. This reaction is commonly used in the hydrogenation of vegetable oils using a nickel catalyst. Vegetable oils generally have long unsaturated carbon chains while animal fats have saturated carbon chains. Animal fats generally contain saturated fatty acids which are said to be harmful for health. Oils containing unsaturated fatty acids should be chosen for cooking.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: What is a substitution reaction? Explain with methane and chlorine.
question_hinglish: Substitution reaction kya hai? Methane aur chlorine se samjhao.
answer_english:
Saturated hydrocarbons are fairly unreactive, but in the presence of sunlight, chlorine reacts with them very fast and replaces hydrogen atoms one by one:
CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl (in sunlight)
It is called a substitution reaction because one type of atom or group takes the place of another. With higher alkanes, a number of products usually form.
answer_hinglish:
Saturated hydrocarbons kaafi kam reactive hote hain, par dhoop mein chlorine unke saath bahut tezi se react karke hydrogen atoms ko ek-ek karke badal deti hai:
CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl (dhoop mein)
Ise substitution reaction kehte hain kyunki ek prakaar ka atom ya group doosre ki jagah leta hai. Bade alkanes ke saath aam taur pe kai products bante hain.
ncert_context: Saturated hydrocarbons are fairly unreactive and are inert in the presence of most reagents. However, in the presence of sunlight, chlorine is added to hydrocarbons in a very fast reaction. Chlorine can replace the hydrogen atoms one by one. It is called a substitution reaction because one type of atom or a group of atoms takes the place of another. A number of products are usually formed with the higher homologues of alkanes. CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl (in the presence of sunlight).

Saturated hydrocarbons are fairly unreactive and are inert in the presence of most reagents. However, in the presence of sunlight, chlorine is added to hydrocarbons in a very fast reaction. Chlorine can replace the hydrogen atoms one by one. It is called a substitution reaction because one type of atom or a group of atoms takes the place of another. A number of products are usually formed with the higher homologues of alkanes. CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl (in the presence of sunlight).

Question:
Substitution reaction kya hai? Methane aur chlorine se samjhao.

Intent Type: explain_concept
Answer the question in Hinglish using only the given context.

Saturated hydrocarbons kaafi kam reactive hote hain, par dhoop mein chlorine unke saath bahut tezi se react karke hydrogen atoms ko ek-ek karke badal deti hai:
CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl (dhoop mein)
Ise substitution reaction kehte hain kyunki ek prakaar ka atom ya group doosre ki jagah leta hai. Bade alkanes ke saath aam taur pe kai products bante hain.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: List the properties and uses of ethanol.
question_hinglish: Ethanol ke gun aur upyog batao.
answer_english:
1. Ethanol is a liquid at room temperature (melting point 156 K, boiling point 351 K), commonly called alcohol.
2. It is the active ingredient of all alcoholic drinks.
3. Being a good solvent, it is used in medicines such as tincture iodine, cough syrups and tonics.
4. It is soluble in water in all proportions.
5. It is an important industrial solvent, and is added to petrol as a cleaner fuel that gives only CO₂ and water on burning.
answer_hinglish:
1. Ethanol room temperature pe liquid hai (melting point 156 K, boiling point 351 K), aur aam taur pe alcohol kehlaata hai.
2. Yeh saare alcoholic drinks ka mukhya ghatak hai.
3. Achha solvent hone se tincture iodine, cough syrup aur tonics jaisi dawaiyon mein use hota hai.
4. Yeh paani mein har anupaat mein ghulta hai.
5. Yeh ek mahatvapurn industrial solvent hai, aur petrol mein saaf fuel ki tarah milaaya jaata hai jo jalne pe sirf CO₂ aur paani deta hai.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: Write the reactions of ethanol with sodium and with excess concentrated sulphuric acid at 443 K.
question_hinglish: Ethanol ki sodium ke saath aur 443 K pe zyada gaadhe sulphuric acid ke saath reactions likho.
answer_english:
With sodium, ethanol gives sodium ethoxide and hydrogen gas:
2Na + 2CH₃CH₂OH → 2CH₃CH₂ONa + H₂
Heated at 443 K with excess concentrated sulphuric acid, ethanol is dehydrated to ethene:
CH₃CH₂OH → CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O
Here concentrated sulphuric acid acts as a dehydrating agent, removing water from ethanol.
answer_hinglish:
Sodium ke saath ethanol sodium ethoxide aur hydrogen gas deta hai:
2Na + 2CH₃CH₂OH → 2CH₃CH₂ONa + H₂
443 K pe zyada gaadhe sulphuric acid ke saath garam karne pe ethanol se paani nikal kar ethene banta hai:
CH₃CH₂OH → CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O
Yahan gaadha sulphuric acid dehydrating agent hai, jo ethanol se paani hatata hai.

With ethanol, the other product is sodium ethoxide. (ii) Reaction to give unsaturated hydrocarbon: Heating ethanol at 443 K with excess concentrated sulphuric acid results in the dehydration of ethanol to give ethene – CH₃CH₂OH → CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O (hot conc. H₂SO₄). The concentrated sulphuric acid can be regarded as a dehydrating agent which removes water from ethanol.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: How do alcohols affect living beings? Why is methanol dangerous, and what is denatured alcohol?
question_hinglish: Alcohols jeevit praaniyon ko kaise prabhaavit karte hain? Methanol khatarnaak kyun hai, aur denatured alcohol kya hai?
answer_english: Large amounts of ethanol slow metabolic processes and depress the central nervous system, causing lack of coordination, mental confusion, drowsiness and finally stupor; even a small amount of pure ethanol (absolute alcohol) can be lethal. Methanol in very small quantities can cause death: it is oxidised to methanal in the liver, which coagulates protoplasm, and it affects the optic nerve, causing blindness. Denatured alcohol is industrial ethanol made unfit to drink by adding poisonous substances like methanol, and coloured blue with dyes for easy identification.
answer_hinglish: Zyada ethanol metabolism dheema karta hai aur central nervous system ko dabaata hai, jisse taalmel ki kami, maansik uljhan, neend aur ant mein behoshi hoti hai; shuddh ethanol (absolute alcohol) ki thodi maatra bhi jaanleva ho sakti hai. Methanol ki bahut thodi maatra bhi maut ka kaaran ban sakti hai: liver mein yeh methanal mein oxidise hota hai jo protoplasm ko jama deta hai, aur yeh optic nerve ko nuksaan pahunchakar andhapan laata hai. Denatured alcohol woh industrial ethanol hai jise methanol jaise zehreele padaarth milakar peene layak nahi rakha jaata, aur aasaani se pehchanne ke liye rang daal kar neela kiya jaata hai.
ncert_context: Intake of even a small quantity of pure ethanol (called absolute alcohol) can be lethal. When large quantities of ethanol are consumed, it tends to slow metabolic processes and to depress the central nervous system. This results in lack of coordination, mental confusion, drowsiness, lowering of the normal inhibitions, and finally stupor. Unlike ethanol, intake of methanol in very small quantities can cause death. Methanol is oxidised to methanal in the liver. Methanal reacts rapidly with the components of cells. It coagulates the protoplasm, in much the same way an egg is coagulated by cooking. Methanol also affects the optic nerve, causing blindness. To prevent the misuse of ethanol produced for industrial use, it is made unfit for drinking by adding poisonous substances like methanol to it. Dyes are also added to colour the alcohol blue so that it can be identified easily. This is called denatured alcohol.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: What is vinegar? Why is pure ethanoic acid called glacial acetic acid, and how strong an acid is it?
question_hinglish: Vinegar kya hai? Shuddh ethanoic acid ko glacial acetic acid kyun kehte hain, aur yeh kitna strong acid hai?
answer_english: Ethanoic acid (acetic acid) is a carboxylic acid; a 5–8% solution of it in water is vinegar, used as a preservative in pickles. Pure ethanoic acid melts at 290 K, so it often freezes in winter in cold climates, giving it the name glacial acetic acid. Unlike mineral acids such as HCl, which are completely ionised, carboxylic acids are weak acids.
answer_hinglish: Ethanoic acid (acetic acid) ek carboxylic acid hai; paani mein iska 5–8% solution vinegar hai, jo achaar mein preservative ki tarah use hota hai. Shuddh ethanoic acid 290 K pe pighalta hai, isliye thandi jagahon pe sardi mein aksar jam jaata hai, isi se iska naam glacial acetic acid pada. HCl jaise mineral acids jo poori tarah ionise hote hain, unke ulat carboxylic acids weak acids hain.
ncert_context: Ethanoic acid is commonly called acetic acid and belongs to a group of acids called carboxylic acids. 5-8% solution of acetic acid in water is called vinegar and is used widely as a preservative in pickles. The melting point of pure ethanoic acid is 290 K and hence it often freezes during winter in cold climates. This gave rise to its name glacial acetic acid. The group of organic compounds called carboxylic acids are obviously characterised by their acidic nature. However, unlike mineral acids like HCl, which are completely ionised, carboxylic acids are weak acids.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: What is esterification? What is saponification?
question_hinglish: Esterification kya hai? Saponification kya hai?
answer_english:
Esterification: ethanoic acid reacts with absolute ethanol in the presence of an acid catalyst to form an ester:
CH₃COOH + CH₃CH₂OH → CH₃COOCH₂CH₃ + H₂O (acid)
Esters are generally sweet-smelling and used in perfumes and as flavouring agents.
Saponification: an ester treated with sodium hydroxide is converted back to alcohol and the sodium salt of the carboxylic acid:
CH₃COOC₂H₅ + NaOH → C₂H₅OH + CH₃COONa
It is called saponification because it is used to make soap.
answer_hinglish:
Esterification: ethanoic acid acid catalyst ki maujoodgi mein absolute ethanol ke saath react karke ester banata hai:
CH₃COOH + CH₃CH₂OH → CH₃COOCH₂CH₃ + H₂O (acid)
Esters aam taur pe meethi khushboo wale hote hain aur perfumes aur flavouring agents mein use hote hain.
Saponification: ester ko sodium hydroxide ke saath kriya karne pe woh waapas alcohol aur carboxylic acid ke sodium salt mein badal jaata hai:
CH₃COOC₂H₅ + NaOH → C₂H₅OH + CH₃COONa
Ise saponification kehte hain kyunki yeh saabun banane mein use hota hai.
ncert_context: Esterification reaction: Esters are most commonly formed by reaction of an acid and an alcohol. Ethanoic acid reacts with absolute ethanol in the presence of an acid catalyst to give an ester – CH₃COOH + CH₃CH₂OH → CH₃COOCH₂CH₃ (ester) + H₂O (acid). Generally, esters are sweet-smelling substances. These are used in making perfumes and as flavouring agents. On treating with sodium hydroxide, which is an alkali, the ester is converted back to alcohol and sodium salt of carboxylic acid. This reaction is known as saponification because it is used in the preparation of soap: CH₃COOC₂H₅ + NaOH → C₂H₅OH + CH₃COONa. Soaps are sodium or potassium salts of long chain carboxylic acid.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: Explain the cleansing action of soap. What is a micelle?
question_hinglish: Saabun ki safaai karne ki kriya samjhao. Micelle kya hai?
answer_english: Most dirt is oily and does not dissolve in water. A soap molecule, a sodium or potassium salt of a long-chain carboxylic acid, has a hydrophilic ionic end that interacts with water and a hydrophobic hydrocarbon tail that interacts with oil. In water, soap molecules form clusters called micelles, with the tails inside around the oily dirt and the ionic ends outside facing water. The micelles stay in solution as a colloid and do not come together because of ion-ion repulsion, so the trapped dirt is rinsed away. Micelles are large enough to scatter light, so soap solution looks cloudy.
answer_hinglish: Zyadatar mail tailiya hota hai aur paani mein nahi ghulta. Saabun ka molecule, jo lambi chain wale carboxylic acid ka sodium ya potassium salt hai, ek hydrophilic ionic sira rakhta hai jo paani se judta hai aur ek hydrophobic hydrocarbon poonchh jo tel se judti hai. Paani mein saabun ke molecules micelles naam ke gucchhe banate hain, jinme poonchhein andar tailiya mail ke chaaron or aur ionic sire bahar paani ki taraf hote hain. Micelles colloid ki tarah solution mein rehte hain aur ion-ion pratikarshan se aapas mein nahi judte, isliye phansa mail dhul jaata hai. Micelles roshni bikherne layak bade hote hain, isliye saabun ka ghol dhundhla dikhta hai.
ncert_context: Most dirt is oily in nature and oil does not dissolve in water. The molecules of soap are sodium or potassium salts of long-chain carboxylic acids. The ionic-end of soap interacts with water while the carbon chain interacts with oil. The soap molecules thus form structures called micelles where one end of the molecules is towards the oil droplet while the ionic-end faces outside. This forms an emulsion in water. Soaps are molecules in which the two ends have differing properties, one is hydrophilic, that is, it interacts with water, while the other end is hydrophobic, that is, it interacts with hydrocarbons. Clusters of molecules in which the hydrophobic tails are in the interior of the cluster and the ionic ends are on the surface of the cluster form a micelle. The oily dirt will be collected in the centre of the micelle. The micelles stay in solution as a colloid and will not come together to precipitate because of ion-ion repulsion. The soap micelles are large enough to scatter light. Hence a soap solution appears cloudy.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: Why does soap form scum with hard water? How are detergents better?
question_hinglish: Kathor paani ke saath saabun scum kyun banata hai? Detergents behtar kaise hain?
answer_english: Soap reacts with calcium and magnesium salts that cause hardness of water, forming an insoluble substance called scum; foam forms with difficulty and more soap is needed. Detergents are generally sodium salts of sulphonic acids or ammonium salts with chloride or bromide ions, with long hydrocarbon chains. Their charged ends do not form insoluble precipitates with calcium and magnesium ions, so they stay effective in hard water. They are used in shampoos and clothes-cleaning products.
answer_hinglish: Saabun paani ki kathorta ke zimmedar calcium aur magnesium salts ke saath react karke scum naam ka na ghulne wala padaarth banata hai; jhaag mushkil se banta hai aur zyada saabun lagta hai. Detergents aam taur pe sulphonic acids ke sodium salts ya chloride ya bromide ions wale ammonium salts hain, jinki lambi hydrocarbon chains hoti hain. Inke charged sire calcium aur magnesium ions ke saath na ghulne wale precipitate nahi banate, isliye yeh kathor paani mein bhi kaam karte hain. Inka use shampoo aur kapde dhone ke products mein hota hai.
ncert_context: Have you ever observed while bathing that foam is formed with difficulty and an insoluble substance (scum) remains after washing with water? This is caused by the reaction of soap with the calcium and magnesium salts, which cause the hardness of water. Hence you need to use a larger amount of soap. This problem is overcome by using another class of compounds called detergents as cleansing agents. Detergents are generally sodium salts of sulphonic acids or ammonium salts with chlorides or bromides ions, etc. Both have long hydrocarbon chain. The charged ends of these compounds do not form insoluble precipitates with the calcium and magnesium ions in hard water. Thus, they remain effective in hard water. Detergents are usually used to make shampoos and products for cleaning clothes.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: While cooking, if the bottom of the vessel is getting blackened on the outside, it means that: (a) the food is not cooked completely (b) the fuel is not burning completely (c) the fuel is wet (d) the fuel is burning completely
question_hinglish: Khaana banate waqt agar bartan ka tala bahar se kaala ho raha hai, toh iska matlab hai: (a) khaana poora nahi pakka (b) fuel poora nahi jal raha (c) fuel geela hai (d) fuel poora jal raha hai
answer_english: (b) The fuel is not burning completely. Blackening means the stove's air holes are blocked, causing incomplete combustion that deposits soot and wastes fuel.
answer_hinglish: (b) Fuel poora nahi jal raha. Kaala hona batata hai ki stove ke hawa ke chhed band hain, jisse adhoora jalna hota hai, kaalikh jamti hai aur fuel barbaad hota hai.
ncert_context: The gas/kerosene stove used at home has inlets for air so that a sufficiently oxygen-rich mixture is burnt to give a clean blue flame. If you observe the bottoms of cooking vessels getting blackened, it means that the air holes are blocked and fuel is getting wasted. Limiting the supply of air results in incomplete combustion even of saturated hydrocarbons giving a sooty flame. Incomplete combustion gives soot which is carbon.

subject: Chemistry
question_english: Assertion (A): Covalent compounds are generally poor conductors of electricity. Reason (R): In covalent compounds, electrons are shared between atoms and no charged particles are formed. Choose: (i) Both true, R explains A (ii) Both true, R does not explain A (iii) A true, R false (iv) A false, R true
question_hinglish: Assertion (A): Covalent compounds aam taur pe bijli ke kharaab conductor hote hain. Reason (R): Covalent compounds mein atoms ke beech electrons share hote hain aur koi charged kan nahi bante. Chuno: (i) Dono sahi, R A ko samjhata hai (ii) Dono sahi, R A ko nahi samjhata (iii) A sahi, R galat (iv) A galat, R sahi
answer_english: (i) Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A. Conduction needs charged particles that can move; since covalent bonding shares electrons and forms no ions, these compounds conduct electricity poorly.
answer_hinglish: (i) A aur R dono sahi hain, aur R A ko sahi samjhata hai. Bijli conduct karne ke liye ghoomne wale charged kan chahiye; covalent bonding mein electrons share hote hain aur ions nahi bante, isliye yeh compounds bijli kharaab conduct karte hain.
ncert_context: Such bonds which are formed by the sharing of an electron pair between two atoms are known as covalent bonds. Covalently bonded molecules are seen to have strong bonds within the molecule, but intermolecular forces are weak. Since the electrons are shared between atoms and no charged particles are formed, such covalent compounds are generally poor conductors of electricity. Most carbon compounds are poor conductors of electricity; we can conclude that the bonding in these compounds does not give rise to any ions.
